Breaking: These 14 Latest Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1493 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • Industry observers note that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this patch isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 newly introduced features—including one feature the manufacturer trialed in the previous beta.

Industry observers note that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger complications. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this new feature here.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 also comes with a new setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? At the moment, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the substantial screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

It has been revealed that with watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

In a recent development, with iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

Sources indicate that the company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these fresh Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Industry observers note that despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

Industry observers note that iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

Industry observers note that for example, you could ask Siri AI to help you blueprint a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Industry observers note that apple started testing its latest Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Industry observers note that continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a latest Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training proposal. You can customize these prepares to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Industry observers note that apple is also testing a newly introduced Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Industry observers note that another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing latest StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with significant iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability at the moment works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out upcoming languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

Recent findings suggest that if you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with just over a week before Fortnite Treasure Hunters comes to an end, desperation has set in, as players begin to lose hope of finding the Pirate Shop Access token. This is the most coveted item in Fortnite history because it grants up to 28 days of free Item Shop cosmetics.

Recent findings suggest that the long search for the token has driven players to cheat. Epic Games has managed to catch these cheaters red-handed and has publicly announced that it will be banning them from Fortnite.

According to recent reports, the consequences aren't limited to the players who resorted to cheating software. Players who win the token by teaming up with a cheater will not be banned, but they will be stripped of the token as well as any Item Shop goodies they claimed while it was active — even if they were unaware that a person in their party cheated. Players who teamed up with the cheater via Squad Fills are the only exception. This measure aims to prevent players from creating a smurf account exclusively for cheating.

It has been revealed that the Pirate Shop Access token may be a reward that's almost too good to be true, but it's also extremely rare. The odds of finding the token are low (0.000007273%). Some players have opened over 150,000 chests with no luck, so it can definitely be frustrating to continue on. Players' best bet is to keep searching and collect other treasure from chests along the way.

According to recent reports, with Golden Week coming up on Nov. 28, players will at least have increased chances of finding the rare gilded skins. Additionally, the week-long event begins on Saturday, when the final Treasure Hours of the season will be active, cranking up token odds by 1.5x. Fortnite Treasure Hunters ends on Dec. 5, so players still have some time to open chests and get the token before it's vaulted for good.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ah, the Bulgarian split squat. Feared by many, loathed by most, but loved by personal trainers all over the world. What if I told you that you'd enjoy this lower-body exercise infinitely more if you followed three simple steps to fix up your form?

It's surprisingly easy to make mistakes with this leg-day exercise, and really, it can be adjusted to be more quad-dominant or glute-dominant — but there are clear signs of bad form, and many more people than you'd think end up on the physical therapy couch because of poor lifting mechanics.

In a recent development, to maximize the benefits of this weightlifting exercise, I recommend learning how to do the Bulgarian split squat before bad habits set in. As a trainer, I have a few tips to help you. Scroll on to see if you're making these common mistakes below and my top tips to fix your form fast.

A post shared by Tom's Guide Fitness | Workout Tips & Gear (@tomsguidefitness).

It's a compound exercise and a part of functional training workouts and strength programs everywhere, helping you build strength and muscle in your glutes, hips, quads, hamstrings and core.

It has been revealed that the move requires balance and coordination, while your upper body, core and hips help stabilize you as you move. But people tend to think of this move as more quads than glutes, which isn't exactly the case.

Here's what I see go wrong, and three quick fixes:.

It has been revealed that in short, you're wasting your time if your form is badly off. And we're busy humans who don't like our time being wasted, right?

Leaning back too far removes tension from the working muscles and overloads your lower back. Keep your torso static and stable — don't hunch or allow your knees to cave inward. That means engaging your core and using the power of your core, glutes and legs to drive movement.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Next, think about your gravity; as I mentioned, keep your back straight and slightly hinge forward to help engage the glutes on your standing leg. If you work with a weight in your opposite hand, this will engage more of the outer glutes, or gluteus medius.

Taking time during the eccentric contraction means slowing down the lowering phase; you can then press upward with power while maximizing tension. It's now thought, due to advances in research, that eccentric contraction is vital for muscle growth and braking force.

If you have an injury, pre-existing health conditions, or you experience pain, speak with a qualified personal trainer or physician first.

  • "I knew we were definitely going to have an opportunity to lay our own track, because — it's right in the title, the fact that you're so many years past 2049, it gives you enough space to really carve out your own identity.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it's impossible enough to have to live in the shadow of an unabashed classic of cinema, so just imagine dealing with two of them. There aren't many who would have a bad word to say about Ridley Scott's original "Blade Runner (well, except for those unfortunate critics who dismissed it upon release), but Denis Villeneuve's highly-acclaimed sequel "Blade Runner 2049" ain't too shabby, either. Now, Prime Video's "Blade Runner 2099" series has the added responsibility of picking up the story where its beloved predecessors left off ... along with all the pressure that comes with that.

For showrunner Silka Luisa, this could've required one of two different approaches: stay suffocatingly faithful to the look and feel and tone of the two films or purposefully set off in the opposite direction. Well, in this case, how about a secret third option instead? During a recent press junket for "Blade Runner 2099," I spoke with Luisa over Zoom about where this show fits in next to its movie kin and how it finds its own niche amid a much wider world:.

"I knew we were definitely going to have an opportunity to lay our own track, because — it's right in the title, the fact that you're so many years past 2049, it gives you enough space to really carve out your own identity.".

Impressively, Luisa looked to Villeneuve's 2017 movie to figure out the ideal way to do just that. "What was so fantastic about what Denis did with '2049' was, he didn't just rehash what Ridley had done," the showrunner told me. "He really created his own take on 'Blade Runner' that is very much his aesthetic. But it still felt like an evolution of Ridley's conversation." In effect, the key was to thread that very tricky needle for "2099.".

When it comes to the recent trend of legacy sequels that have dominated the last decade or so of franchise filmmaking, it can certainly feel like we can count the worthwhile ones on just one or two hands. Fortunately, for Silka Luisa and her creative team on "Blade Runner 2099," Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049" is basically the poster child for legacy sequels done right. Rather than simply retread all the same ground as before (looking at you, "Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens"), "Blade Runner 2049" moved the story forward and took some seriously big risks along the way.

According to Luisa, this gave her all the permission she needed to follow in its footsteps and take things in bold fresh directions with her show. "That freed us up in a lot of different ways, because it meant we weren't just beholden to repeating the same thing over and over again," she explains. One massive wrinkle in the Prime Video series is the fact "Blade Runner 2099" takes place after a Replicant uprising has shaken up the status quo, putting humans at the bottom of the food chain for once. It's a strange dynamic that our two main characters Olwen (the Replicant Blade Runner played by Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (the human posing as a Replicant played by Hunter Schafer) are forced to navigate throughout the season.

As fans tune in, they can rest assured in the knowledge that the series is taking its cues from one of the most ambitious and boundary-pushing legacy sequels of them all. You could do a lot worse than that. All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are now on Prime Video.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that johansson is teaming up with Mike Flanagan for the latest reboot of the classic horror franchise, starring as Latest York City homicide detective Julie Miller as she is pulled into a dark murder investigation with apparent ties to a former Satanic serial killer she helped stop.
  • Now, with just over two months until it hits theaters, the Motion Picture Association has officially given The Exorcist: Martyrs an R rating, continuing the horror franchise's 53-year streak of landing the mature rating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scarlett Johansson's The Exorcist: Martyrs will be pulling no punches.

Industry observers note that johansson is teaming up with Mike Flanagan for the latest reboot of the classic horror franchise, starring as Latest York City homicide detective Julie Miller as she is pulled into a dark murder investigation with apparent ties to a former Satanic serial killer she helped stop. Also starring Chiwetel Ejiofor, Diane Lane, Jacobi Jupe and Sasha Lane, among many others, The Exorcist: Martyrs is currently on track for a March 12 release date.

Now, with just over two months until it hits theaters, the Motion Picture Association has officially given The Exorcist: Martyrs an R rating, continuing the horror franchise's 53-year streak of landing the mature rating. The site further explains that the new reboot's rating stems from its "bloody violent content, grisly images, language, and some sexual references.".

Recent findings suggest that in addition to the franchise's tradition, The Exorcist: Martyrs securing an R-rating also continues Flanagan's streak of more mature films in the director's chair. Across his eight released films, only two have landed a PG-13 rating from the MPA, those being Netflix's Before I Wake and Blumhouse's Ouija: Origin of Evil. His TV highlights have similarly landed firmly in the TV-MA rating, generally stemming from explicit language and, in recent years, some bloodier set pieces.

Interestingly, while it keeps the series' 53-year streak alive, The Exorcist: Martyr's R-rating does immediately stand out from its predecessors with its promise of "grisly images." Though the horror franchise is well-known for its more visceral material, the only other movie to explicitly list its gruesome imagery as part of its R-rating was that of the infamous Exorcist: The Beginning prequel film. See the chart below for the full franchise list of ratings and given reasons from the MPA:.

Strong language and disturbing images.

Exorcist II: The Heretic (1977).

Strong violence and gore, disturbing images and rituals, and for language including some sexual dialogue.

Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist (2005).

Strong violence and disturbing images.

Some violent content, disturbing images, language and sexual references.

Bloody violent content, grisly images, language, and some sexual references.

The first Exorcist: Martyrs trailer already showcased Flanagan leaning into more gruesome territory for his reboot of the classic horror series. The crime scenes Johansson's character inspects come complete with dead bodies mutilated in different ritualistic manners, while another sequence saw Julie inspecting a barrel later with an unknown entity emerging and coated in blood. As Flanagan himself teased to ScreenRant, he was not looking to pull any punches with his film, calling it "very, very bloody":.

Mike Flanagan: Yeah, I think the only thing that comes close to the amount of blood is we did melt that orgy in The Fall of the House of Usher in acid. That was pretty bloody, but that was funny, I thought. [Chuckles] As dark as it was, this is vicious, and that isn't a muscle I get to flex very often. It's very disturbing, and that was part of the fun of it. This whole story just felt very unsafe from the beginning, and yeah, that isn't a gear I go toward frequently. I like hope and heart and humanism, and there are moments of that if you squint, but this is a dark story, and it is scary. So yeah, that was very exciting for me, too.

Industry observers note that with Flanagan also having been largely inspired by the cult favorite Exorcist III for his take on the franchise, it will be interesting to see if The Exorcist: Martyrs finds itself leaning closer to the 1990 film's atmosphere than the visceral nature of its 2004 successor. Given early test screenings, per the director, have been glowing, as has the response to the trailer thus far, it does at least seem like this push into hard-R territory is going to give viewers an unforgettable experience.

Thirteen years after stopping a satanic serial killer, New York City detective Julie Miller confronts a new murderer who appears connected to her past. With help from a former prison chaplain and a rookie detective, she investigates a sinister connection between history's most notorious killers.

Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

  • Sources indicate that “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” and, by extension, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” occupy a unique place in Tarantino’s cinematic world, as they’re both part of his so-called “Realer Than Real World Universe” and his “Movie Movie Universe.” Tarantino didn’t just keep crafting his movies-within-movies world with the hit film — he also introduced real-world (realer than real world?) elements and people (the Manson Family, of course, and all that entails).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: This article contains small spoilers for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”].

It should come as little surprise that David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” focuses on, well, Cliff Booth. The Quentin Tarantino-penned sequel to the filmmaker’s own 2019 Oscar-winning hit “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” has always been billed as a spinoff following the continuing adventures of his fictitious (yet still iconic) stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt). But Tarantino has always loved building out his own shared and connected universe(s), and fans sure love exploring its outer limits.

Sources indicate that “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” and, by extension, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” occupy a unique place in Tarantino’s cinematic world, as they’re both part of his so-called “Realer Than Real World Universe” and his “Movie Movie Universe.” Tarantino didn’t just keep crafting his movies-within-movies world with the hit film — he also introduced real-world (realer than real world?) elements and people (the Manson Family, of course, and all that entails). Related Stories ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March ‘The Trip’ Returns for Fifth Installment, Next Sending Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon to Frigid Arctic Circle.

According to recent reports, that bent continues in “Cliff Booth,” which is rife with both out-there elements and very real references (time for that “Hee Haw” resurgence, we guess). But the film also has to follow its own series logic, which means, yes, it’s the Cliff Booth show, but hey, where are our “Hollywood” co-stars Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie)?

[Once again: This article contains small spoilers for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”].

It has been revealed that when we first meet Cliff and Rick, the duo are long-time colleagues and best pals. As his stunt double, Cliff is tasked with doing some serious heavy lifting for Hollywood star Rick, which inevitably (?) leads them to off four members of the Manson Family. The raucous and wild violence the duo inflicts on the foursome isn’t just a fun bonding exercise for the pair. It also ensures that the nefarious group can’t go next door to enact the infamous (and very real) Tate murders. Win-win!

Sources indicate that the film ends with an invitation for Rick to slide on over to the Tate house for a thank-you drink, presumably putting him in the path of Roman Polanski, Sharon, and all the star power they carry. “Cliff Booth” is set eight years after those events, and while Rick may have enjoyed a career upswing in the interim, his current professional endeavors have taken him far from Hollywood.

While we never see Rick in the film (despite ongoing rumors that DiCaprio might appear for a quick cameo), Cliff mentions him frequently and fondly, including telling potential paramour Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki) that their professional entanglements ended when Rick got, ahem, “too fat” for Cliff to believably double him and then moved to Australia to star in the TV series “Dingo Dan.” Further details on the show are slim, but we do know it’s a Western TV show that’s proven quite popular and durable (Aussie Karen seems to like it), and Cliff makes it sound like Rick is enjoying himself. Not too bad.

By blending his two movie universes with “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” Tarantino got to both delight in late-’60s Hollywood magic and “save” Sharon Tate, her unborn son, Abigail Folger, Wojciech Frykowski, Steven Parent, and Jay Sebring. That sort of revisionist history was the film’s buzziest twist and, as I argued at the time, the most emotional choice Tarantino has ever made in his filmography.

And while we don’t get treated to much more Sharon in “Cliff Booth,” we are granted some, in the form of a Red Apple Cigarettes commercial led by a beaming Margot Robbie, returning to her original role as the doomed actress. (The fake cigarettes are another Tarantino-verse staple, and Rick even appears in his own commercial for them during the end credits of “Hollywood.”).

It has been revealed that in the short cameo, Sharon looks healthy and happy, and she’s clearly still enough of a star to warrant her own advertising campaign, built on her smile and her zippy shimmy. As Cliff watches the commercial at the Marina del Rey condo he shares with his dad (Peter Weller), he takes the time to stop, observe, and notably smile at the star. It’s a small grace note, and a very effective one.

Industry observers note that one other star of “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” is missing from “Cliff Booth,” though. Just where the heck is Brandy?

Netflix will release “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” in IMAX theaters on Wednesday, November 25. It will be available to stream on Netflix starting Wednesday, December 23.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • What are the best games on PlayStation 5?
  • It has been revealed that that aside, the PS5's library has grown to the extent that there's a lot to sort through, and fresh and old PS5 owners will be wondering what to play.
  • Our latest enhancement to this list on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What are the best games on PlayStation 5? Hard as it is to believe, the PS5 is — by Sony's own admission — already well past the halfway point of its life-cycle. (It's even time to start thinking about PS6.) It's fair to say that PS5 hasn't been deluged with classics, and the rate of must-play new releases is slower than it has been on previous PlayStations. But it does now have the ultimate killer app: Grand Theft Auto 6.

It has been revealed that that aside, the PS5's library has grown to the extent that there's a lot to sort through, and fresh and old PS5 owners will be wondering what to play. So here’s our living list of the best video games we’ve played on the platform — influenced by the personal tastes of the Polygon team — to be updated as more games come out.

Our latest enhancement to this list on Nov. 25 added Grand Theft Auto 6.

The Polygon staff plays a lot of video games, and everything in this list comes personally recommended by at least one of us. We determined what should be on our list of the best PlayStation 5 games by looking at the quality of each title, but also with an eye for breadth and variety — so you should find something on the list you’ll enjoy, no matter what genres of game you like, how much time you have, or what vibe you are after.

Sources indicate that A full six years into the PS5's life, here it is: the game that finally makes sense of this console generation, and makes it all worthwhile. GTA 6 is the best-reviewed game of all time, and you don't have to spend long with it to understand why. It's a deeply engrossing world of astonishing detail, reactivity, and scope, rendered in all the seedy, dayglo glamor that can be mustered by the most expensive video game production of all time. It's a familiarly scattershot satire of modern life in America. But — and it's a huge but — it's also a game of real sensitivity and heart. The central couple of Jason and Lucia are straight-up adorable and Rockstar indicates, for the first time in the series' history, a moving willingness to see the best in people. Well... some people. —OW.

Read Giovanni Colantonio's full review of Grand Theft Auto 6.

It has been revealed that if you're craving a return to the days of Wipeout, when a PlayStation racing game was as likely to involve antigravity sci-fi craft rocketing around at hundreds of miles per hour as realistic cars, then Galactic Racer is the game for you. It also happens to be one of the most innovative racing games in a long time, a much-needed shake-up for a stale genre. It introduces a roguelite structure and build-crafting into both single-player and even multiplayer modes, while keeping it all totally coherent with a very Star Wars fantasy of racing dangerous, rickety hot rods. As a treat, there's a healthy dose of Burnout in there, too. —Oli Welsh.

Read Oli Welsh's full review of Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

It has been revealed that here's another classic PlayStation flavor resurrected in an unexpectedly glorious way. As the latest in Bandai Namco's long-running dogfighting air combat series, Ace Combat 8 sounds like a niche known quantity. Try it, however, and you'll be pleasantly surprised again and again: by the sophistication of the controls, the variety of the level design, the meaty length of the campaign, the amazing fidelity of the visuals, and the depth and seriousness of its operatic wartime storyline. —OW.

Read Giovanni Colantonio's full review of Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve.

The PS5 generation has been a bit short on really great tactics games, but that's all changed with this superb squad strategy game from Bit Reactor, set during Star Wars' Clone Wars era. Many on the team worked on Firaxis' XCOM reboot games, and you can sure tell — this is fine-honed game design full of precision, personality, puzzle-like ingenuity, and just the right amount of unpredictability. Zero Tech giant also makes brilliant use of its setting, compellingly painting a grunt's-eye-view of the collapse of the Republic, and assembling a squad of characters you'll really care about. Especially when you lose them forever in the default permadeath setting. —OW.

Read Elijah Gonzalez's full review of Star Wars Zero Firm.

In a recent development, it's been a long time since there was an official James Bond game, and a much longer time — almost 30 years, in fact — since there was a really great one. 007 First Light might not attain the legendary status of GoldenEye 007, but it's a very slick and entertaining blockbuster action game that's a lot smarter than it needed to be. The key is an inspired choice of developer in IO Interactive, of Hitman fame. IO's love of open-ended "social stealth" gameplay sneaks its way in between the set-pieces and rounds out a thoroughly satisfying adventure with a unique perspective on a young Bond. —OW.

Read Ford James' full review of 007 First Light.

Industry observers note that it's defiantly not for everyone, but when the planets align, Bungie's take on the extraction shooter genre can be a totally electrifying multiplayer experience. Its asymmetric PvPvE gameplay can be hard to get your head around, never mind brutally unforgiving, but for intensity and drama it can hardly be matched, and Bungie is to be commended for including interesting solo as well as group roles. On top of this, you have intriguingly deep sci-fi world-building, Bungie's world-class gamefeel — 25 years on from Halo, there are still no more satisfying guns to shoot in gaming — and absolutely stunning art direction, realising one a compellingly chilling future. —OW.

Read Corey Plante's impressions of Marathon.

You can accuse this sequel to Supergiant Games' smash hit roguelike action game of overcomplicating the pure brilliance of the first Hades, and we did. But really this is quibbling with something that's very close to perfection. The combat is still crisp and thrilling, the randomized boons are still exquisitely balanced, the see-saw between progression and setback on each run is still perfectly judged, and the languid, sexy bickering of Supergiant's take on the pantheon of Greek mythology is still gloriously characterful and thirsty. Simply the best that indie gaming has to offer. —OW.

Read Ari Notis' full review of Hades 2.

Sources indicate that capcom has completed a swift one-two punch in early 2026 by following Resident Evil Requiem with an unexpected gem of a sci-fi action game. Like all of Capcom's best work, Pragmata is both a slick, modern blockbuster and steeped in deep, old-school video game vibes. It's a cinematically ambitious game about fatherhood and the AI threat. But also you're a dude in a spacesuit shooting robots on a moon base, eking out your resources and testing your reflexes between save points.

Recent findings suggest that this is a time-honored template (albeit one that makes for a pleasant gear-change in the here and now). Capcom mixes it up with Diana, your childlike android companion, who disrupts both the storytelling and the gameplay in interesting ways. She sweetly draws the best out of the protagonist, Hugh, while potentially fooling both Hugh and the player that she's any different from the AI army they combat. And her hacking ability, which plays out as a grid-based minigame, is Pragmata's chief gameplay innovation; it blends surprisingly compelling quickfire puzzles into the third-person shooting to brilliant effect — so much so that, when you earn the ability to bypass it, you'll probably choose not to. Pragmata plays solidly, looks sharp, and most importantly, feels fresh. It's a class act. —OW.

Read Austin Manchester's full review of Pragmata.

It’s a bold move, on the part of Remedy Entertainment, to actually make a decade-late sequel to a game that defined the studio, but whose ambitions it has arguably outgrown in the years since — particularly in its stunning, architectural action game Control. Might a trip back to Alan Wake’s spooky woods, so obviously haunted by the ghosts of Stephen King and David Lynch, not feel like a step back? Hardly. What Remedy created by bringing all its experience to bear on its most beloved creation is nothing short of a survival horror masterpiece, as well as a meta mystery about its own creation.

Recent findings suggest that horror author Alan is joined by a co-protagonist, FBI agent Saga Anderson, who’s investigating a case linked to Alan’s disappearance over a decade earlier. Using this dual setup — impressively, you can fluidly switch between Alan’s and Saga’s stories essentially at your discretion — Remedy works outward from the original game’s premise, twisting it into a methodical detective thriller one moment and a reality-bending cosmic horror the next. Alan Wake 2 announces the start of a new generation of blockbuster horror gaming. —OW.

Read Toussaint Egan’s full review of Alan Wake 2.

One of the most exciting gaming stories of 2024 has been the elevation of Team Asobi, makers of a series of charming tech demos, to the top flight of Sony’s in-house developers with Astro Bot. Expanding on the free pack-in game Astro’s Playroom, intended as a demo for the capabilities of the DualSense controller, Astro Bot is a dazzling, full-fledged, tour de force platform game capable of standing toe-to-toe with some of Nintendo’s greatest — and it’s surely the best platformer Sony has ever released.

It has been revealed that astro Bot is many things at once. It’s a stunning technical showcase, from the sheen of its ray-traced surfaces to the tippy-tap of the adorable Astro’s footfalls rendered in the DualSense’s haptics and speaker. It’s a nonstop riot of invention that keeps throwing upcoming ideas, gizmos, slapstick interactions, hilarious bosses, and tortuous challenges at you. And — with its hundreds of collectible bots dressed up as PlayStation game characters — it’s a wholehearted, even moving celebration of PlayStation history in the brand’s 30th anniversary year that takes particular care to honor the many wild creations of Japan Studio, the now sadly defunct in-house developer Team Asobi used to call home. It’s poignant to reflect that the time of such creative PlayStation games as Ico, LocoRoco, and PaRappa the Rapper is passed. But it’s joyful to realize that Astro and Team Asobi are here to keep that spirit alive into the future. —OW.

Read Oli Welsh’s full review of Astro Bot.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quentin Tarantino has returned to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" with "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" (why not read our review of the new movie here?).
  • Early in "Cliff Booth," we're introduced to Charlie Peters, a hot-tempered TV star played by Scott Caan.
  • Fans of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" will recall that Tarantino also provided narration in that movie, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quentin Tarantino has returned to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" with "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" (why not read our review of the new movie here?). But this time, while Tarantino penned the script, he isn't in the director's chair. Instead, he's handed directing duties over to his pal David Fincher (who is ending his exclusive deal with Netflix with the film). Tarantino might not be behind the camera, but he still has a presence in the film, and it echoes something he did in "Hollywood" as well.

Early in "Cliff Booth," we're introduced to Charlie Peters, a hot-tempered TV star played by Scott Caan. To speed-run us through Charlie's successful career, we're given a little montage of his various roles, and that montage is narrated by none other than Tarantino, whose very recognizable voice provides some humorous details about Charlie's work.

Fans of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" will recall that Tarantino also provided narration in that movie, too. He actually wasn't the only narrator, either, because during one scene, Kurt Russell, who plays a stuntman named Randy in that film, also provides a little narration. As for Tarantino, he also voiced some crucial narration during a pivotal scene in "The Hateful Eight.".

Sources indicate that in fact, the filmmaker has a history of popping up in his movies, either via a voice cameo or a physical appearance. He has a pretty significant role in "Reservoir Dogs," makes a memorable cameo in "Pulp Fiction," gets to use an abysmal Australian accent in "Django Unchained," has his voice heard during a movie playing in "Inglourious Basterds" (and also plays a corpse in the film), plays a bartender in "Death Proof," portrays one of the members of the Crazy 88 gang in "Kill Bill," and lends his voice to an answering machine in "Jackie Brown.".

So while "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" may not technically be a Quentin Tarantino movie, it still feels like one, right down to the obligatory cameo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, “The Right Stuff” was released 43 years ago, but its spectacular aerial and outer space sequences have lost none of their power. Director Philip Kaufman’s adaptation of Tom Wolfe’s book, which traced the history of the test pilots who became the first astronauts, features immersive set pieces that are still as convincing as ever, in spite of decades of technological advancements since it was made. To revisit it via Criterion‘s fresh 4K UHD physical media release is to experience one of the most groundbreaking and enduring films of all time.

Industry observers note that the new Criterion transfer was supervised by cinematographer Caleb Deschanel, who was still relatively early in his career when Kaufman tapped him to shoot “The Right Stuff.” Deschanel didn’t have many feature credits, but the ones he did have were impressive: his early work included the stunning imagery of “The Black Stallion” and two Hal Ashby movies, “Being There” and the Rolling Stones concert film “Let’s Spend the Night Together.” He would earn the first of his six Academy Award nominations for “The Right Stuff.” Related Stories Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March.

According to recent reports, deschanel had met Kaufman years earlier when Deschanel was a film student at USC, and Kaufman was a young director working on the Western “The Great Northfield Minnesota Raid.” “A couple friends and I put on these rock demonstrates at Shrine Auditorium, and he came to a couple of those,” Deschanel told IndieWire. Deschanel visited the set of “Minnesota” and stayed in touch with Kaufman, who called him around 10 years later with the offer to shoot “The Right Stuff.”.

“It was a dream come true,” Deschanel mentioned, noting that he had always been an aviation buff who loved going to air reveals with his father. He also remembered that Kaufman wasn’t the only person on “The Right Stuff” who he had met years earlier. “Years before we had moved into our first house and needed some painting done, and we had a friend who was teaching in the Cal Arts theater department. He said, ‘I have this actor who’s really great who paints houses in the summer.'”.

According to recent reports, deschanel hired the young actor and got to know him a little bit, and five years later was having lunch with his wife Mary Jo and Kaufman when Kaufman revealed them a picture of the actor he had chosen to play John Glenn. “I said, ‘We know him. That’s Ed Harris. He painted our house,'” Deschanel said. “Then, coincidentally, the woman who was supposed to play Annie Glenn dropped out of and Phil cast my wife, so they ended up playing husband and wife in the movie.”.

One of the great technical challenges of “The Right Stuff” was integrating archival footage of the space race with the new material being shot — one of the reasons the movie was shot in a 1.85:1 aspect ratio instead of a wider Panavision format as one might have expected for such an epic film. “We were using actual footage of NASA’s rocket releases and things like that, and they were filming in the old-fashioned 4:3 format using the full frame of a 35mm camera,” Deschanel stated. “Converting that to widescreen was really impossible.”.

Working in close collaboration with visual effects supervisor Gary Gutierrez (who provides a fascinating look at the film’s miniature and rear-projection work on the Criterion disc), Deschanel solved the numerous logistical problems that came with trying to make it look as though the actors were hurtling through the air at the speed of sound and beyond. Even when Gutierrez thought he had solutions that would work, they often had to be tweaked to accommodate Kaufman’s desire to make everything feel as realistic and immersive as possible.

Early attempts to use a motion-control system for the effects, for example, were discarded because the camera movement was too smooth for Kaufman’s purposes. “Phil wanted it to have some energy to it,” Deschanel said. “That changed the whole methodology.” Whenever rockets were taking off or various crafts were flying, Deschanel made sure to add some shake to the camera. “I actually gave my camera operator, Craig Denault, a black eye at one point because I was hitting the camera so hard.”.

In addition to the expected challenges, there were plenty of unexpected ones as well — like the fact that Sam Shepard, who played ace pilot Chuck Yeager, wouldn’t fly. “The only time he ever went up in an airplane was when Yeager took him for a flight,” Deschanel stated. “Other than that, whenever we had a mockup of an X-1 or the F-104 or anything like that, he’d make me get in and show him how it was going to twist and turn before he would get into it.” For Yeager’s scenes and many of the others, rear projection was used — meaning Deschanel had to photograph what was seen outside the pilots’ and astronauts’ windows long before the actors’ material was actually shot.

It has been revealed that “There was a lot of complexity to all those things,” Deschanel mentioned. “But it gave it a real energy and sense of being there. And that’s what you try to discover as you’re filming any film: what is that visual metaphor that really makes you believe you’re having the same experience the characters are having?” Creating that sense of authenticity required some unorthodox approaches, as when Deschanel had a Learjet pilot take the nose cone off of his plane and replace it with a clear dome.

It has been revealed that “We put a camera in there with a 15mm lens, and then we were able to go up above 50,000 feet,” Deschanel remarked. “At that level, it’s so dark, it’s almost like you’re in outer space. Anything you could think of to find the reality of the movie, we employed.” Deschanel’s perfectionism became the stuff of legend over the years, with some people who worked on “The Right Stuff” claiming he insisted on shooting only at sunrise or sunset to get the most beautiful possible images — a myth Deschanel is quick to dispel.

According to recent reports, “The fact is we shot all day long and had really long days,” Deschanel said. “There was one point where, just to finish up at Edwards Air Force Base, I was on for 24 hours and changed the crew in the middle. So I had a whole fresh crew for the second half of that long day.” That said, Deschanel acknowledges that the film’s justly famous exteriors were important to him, in part for what they represented.

Recent findings suggest that “The iconic moment is when Yeager is on horseback, and he rides up and sees the X-1,” Deschanel stated. “It’s like ‘The Professionals’ or ‘The Wild Bunch,’ these movies about the end of the West as fresh technology takes over. To me, there’s this wonderful representation of the end of an era when Yeager comes across this fighter jet. Then, of course, he flies it and breaks the sound barrier. So it’s this wonderful juxtaposition of notable moments in human history, where one person does something that further advances flight to the point that makes it possible for the next generation to go into outer space. I always miss that I never got to make a Western, but in a way, ‘The Right Stuff’ is a Western.”.

“The Right Stuff” special edition 4K UHD release is now available from Criterion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Streaming platforms are in full swing with live-action video game adaptations, and HBO’s upcoming Baldur’s Gate series is among the most exciting presently in development. Reportedly set after the events of Baldur’s Gate 3, the show looks set to bring one of the most iconic settings from Dungeons & Dragons to the small screen. The city of Baldur’s Gate offers enormous possibilities for a live-action D&D TV show, especially since it follows on from the events of the hugely popular video game series.

Details remain scarce, but for fans of Baldur’s Gate 3, a key question is who will play its beloved characters if they return. Many want original performers such as Neil Newbon and Jennifer English to reprise their roles, and the HBO show’s developer, The Last Of Us’s Craig Mazin, has expressed interest in involving the game’s cast (via Deadline). However, his enthusiasm doesn’t guarantee that they’ll definitely return, or that they’ll play the same characters. Fortunately, there are some more than suitable actors to fill the shoes of any familiar party members returning in HBO’s Baldur’s Gate series.

It has been revealed that astarion can make an appalling suggestion sound like the most entertaining idea in the room. He has a unique combination of elegance, malice, and impeccable comic timing, all of which is familiar territory for Tom Hiddleston, whose performance as Loki made the MCU’s trickster god’s wounded pride and theatrical mischief irresistible. He’s also got prior experience playing a vampire thanks to 2013’s Only Lovers Left Alive. Both roles capture something that’s essential to Astarion: the arrogance of immortality being used to mask a sense of desperation and need for a greater purpose than simply living forever.

In a recent development, tom Hiddleston could deliver Astarion’s most withering remarks with ease while also making the sudden disappearance of that confidence feel just as unsettling in HBO’s Baldur’s Gate TV show as it was in BG3. Any actor playing Astarion requires an understanding of how a charming character can swiftly become a terrifying one. Hiddleston has the skills to make Astarion hilarity land without him being reduced to comic relief. He could make BG3’s vampire rogue funny, unsettling, and emotionally complex, all of which would be essential when following in the footsteps of Neil Newbon’s performance in the game.

Ben Barnes has already shown how fun to watch a charming, articulate man with dangerous magical ambitions can be. His time as General Kirigan/The Darkling in Netflix’s Shadow and Bone is a great glimpse of how he might handle Gale’s susceptibility to power in a live-action Baldur’s Gate story, while The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian demonstrates the sincerity needed for the wizard’s more approachable side. Any actor playing Gale needs to balance both sides for the performance to land.

Recent findings suggest that the greatest challenge if Gale makes an appearance in HBO’s Baldur’s Gate series is ensuring the Wizard of Waterdeep feels approachable despite his intellectual ego. His elaborate explanations and social awkwardness make him considerably warmer than a stereotypical mysterious fantasy sorcerer. Still, this should never mean he comes across as weak or incapable. Roles like Billy Russo in The Punisher prove that Ben Barnes has no issue portraying characters who are charming yet still dangerous, especially those driven by ambitions those around them would struggle to understand.

Recent findings suggest that karlach should look capable of throwing an enemy across a room without breaking a sweat, and WWE superstar Rhea Ripley would make that immediately believable. While not an experienced actor, her wrestling career supplies the strength, explosive movement, and physical confidence needed for a tiefling barbarian who has survived the Blood War. Just as important is her ability to command attention through posture and facial expressions. Ripley can make a grin feel like a challenge or an invitation, a promising quality for a character whose excitement about being alive is just as memorable as her capacity for destruction.

Industry observers note that true, it would be an ambitious move into dramatic acting for Rhea Ripley, especially given how much pain sits beneath Karlach’s enthusiasm. Her infernal engine makes the simple possibility of touching someone devastatingly important, and those scenes demand tenderness as much as rage. Ripley’s suitability for the role lies in the combination of playfulness with being physically intimidating. If she can pull of the more nuanced side of Karlach’s character too, she’ll be more than ideal for HBO’s Baldur’s Gate TV show cast.

According to recent reports, anya Taylor-Joy’s work as the titular road warrior in Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga makes a solid argument for giving her a sword and very little patience in the live-action Baldur’s Gate series. Characters like Furiosa as well as Margot in The Menu are all the evidence needed that she can communicate determination through a fixed stare and a stubborn refusal to show weakness, which is essential for Lae’zel. The Githyanki fighter’s severity comes from a culture that treats strength as survival and obedience as virtue. Taylor-Joy’s filmography leaves little doubt that she could make that conditioning visible in every moment Lae’zel is on-screen.

Industry observers note that anya Taylor-Joy's performance as Beth Harmon in The Queen’s Gambit in particular reveals that she can bring a convincing blend of near-unshakable pride even in the face of profound isolation. Lae’zel’s confidence in her abilities is compelling in BG3 because it survives encounters that dismantle her understanding of the world, and Taylor-Joy would have no issue ensuring this stays intact in a live-action performance. Her penchant for precise delivery would also suit the accidental comedy of Lae’zel’s blunt observations, keeping the humor rooted in the warrior’s absolute conviction that everyone around her is being ridiculous when she finds herself at odds with the room.

Sources indicate that when voiced by Jennifer English in BG3, Shadowheart could make even an admission of ignorance or failure feel like somebody else’s embarrassing mistake. The half-elf cleric needs an actress who can deliver that same sarcasm while also making it clear that keeping those around her at a distance takes effort. Her damaged memories and religious conditioning mean that certainty about her place in the world has to be actively maintained. Fallout, Yellowjackets, and Sweetpea star Ella Purnell could ensure the contradictions that define Shadowheart survive the transition to live-action in HBO’s Baldur’s Gate series.

Sources indicate that viewers should want to understand Shadowheart even when she’s doing something atrocious, a quality Ella Purnell’s performance as Rhiannon in Sweetpea hinges on. Her portrayal of Lucy MacLean in Prime Video’s Fallout series highlights how effectively she can capture someone discovering that the beliefs shaping her life conceal horrifying truths, another essential Shadowheart trait. Finally, her work as Jackie Taylor in Yellowjackets reveals a capacity to capture wounded pride and defensive cruelty. Together, these roles suggest that there are few actresses out there more suited to playing Shadowheart in live-action.

Regé-Jean Page already has experience in projects based on D&D. Not only that, he’s already played a character who exists in the same world as the city of Baldur’s Gate, the Forgotten Realms. As Xenk Yendar in 2023’s Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, Page brought effortless authority and wonderfully straight-faced humor to a hero whose defining personality trait is an unwavering commitment to doing good. Wyll would benefit from that same lack of embarrassment about heroism. While his character is far from simple, Wyll’s most immediate trait is that he sincerely wants to protect people.

Playing Xenk is all the proof needed that Page could make his borderline-theatrical confidence appealing while ensuring his willingness to put himself in danger feels sincere rather than sanctimonious. However, Wyll’s story also offers considerably more internal conflict than Xenk Yendar’s. His pact with the dark entity Mizora directly contradicts his noble intentions. Thankfully, Regé-Jean Page’s Simon Basset in Bridgerton showcased an ability to play polished charm that acts as a mask for concealed vulnerability and self-doubt. That experience would suit Wyll’s complicated relationship with his father and the personal costs of his pact with Mizora.

It has been revealed that few actors have a knack for playing approachable yet believable leadership figures like Anson Mount. His Captain Christopher Pike in Star Trek: Strange New Worlds can command a crisis and then make his colleagues feel comfortable around a dinner table. This is an excellent foundation for playing Halsin in HBO’s Baldur’s Gate series. The archdruid’s imposing appearance comes with an unusually gentle temperament. His experience gives him authority, but he rarely needs to flex his superiority. Mount could bring that reassuring confidence to a BG3 character who feels equally believable offering guidance, expressing desire, or becoming terrifying when someone threatens the vulnerable.

According to recent reports, any actor playing Halsin also needs to create a sense that the Baldur’s Gate character has interests beyond whatever emergency currently occupies the party. His devotion to nature, openness about pleasure, and concern for people damaged by conflict make him earthy and approachable despite his age. Anson Mount’s relaxed warmth would help those qualities emerge naturally, while his more rugged work in Hell on Wheels prove he has the action credentials for the druid’s less peaceful moments. With Halsin, the attraction is partly that strength and safety belong together, and Mount could definitely deliver this.

Long before the adventure in Baldur’s Gate 3 begins, Jaheira had already accumulated enough victories and losses to distrust a promising adventure. The veteran half-elf druid and Harper leader needs a cast member in the live-action Baldur’s Gate series who can bring that world weariness to life without turning every exchange into a solemn lesson. Hollywood veteran Michelle Pfeiffer could inarguably bring that authority, and her skills with dry humor would be just as valuable.

Pfeiffer’s Catwoman in Batman Returns is a perfect demonstration of how she can combine sharp wit with emotional baggage without making one quality cancel out the other. Her work as Lamia in 2007’s Stardust also shows how entertaining she can be in a high-fantasy setting. Jaheira needs a more grounded performance than many other Baldur’s Gate characters, with her sharpness honed by years of experience. Pfeiffer could make a cutting observation feel affectionate or devastating depending on who deserves it, while giving the character’s rarer admissions of grief the emotional weight they need.

Put physical powerhouse Dave Bautista beside a tiny hamster and much of Minsc’s visual appeal is already accounted for. The more crucial qualification is his understanding of how to make an enormous warrior funny through complete sincerity. As Drax in the Guardians of the Galaxy movies, Bautista repeatedly made literal-minded pronouncements entertaining because the character believed them so completely. Minsc needs that same commitment. His conversations with Boo, his miniature giant space hamster companion, should sound perfectly reasonable to him, however bewildered everyone around him becomes.

In a recent development, the BG3 ranger’s uncomplicated commitment to fighting evil would also give Bautista something substantial beneath the comedy. Just like Drax, Minsc’s understanding of a situation may be eccentric, but his love for his friends and determination to protect them are never minor details. Bautista has shown how tenderness can sit within an intimidating physical performance, and he could make those loyalties the reason audiences invest in the character. His size would sell the action immediately; his ability to express hurt or delight with disarming openness could ensure that Minsc remains lovable between the battles, too.

According to recent reports, A quiet threat can be considerably more unnerving than a shouted one, and Rebecca Ferguson’s filmography proves she understands that distinction. Her Lady Jessica in Dune and Dune: Part Two combines controlled authority with a willingness to manipulate events toward ruthless ends. Those qualities would translate beautifully to Minthara, a drow paladin whose noble upbringing and brutal education inform nearly every judgment she makes. Ferguson could convey that instinctive expectation of obedience through her voice and stillness, making Minthara formidable before she ever reaches for a weapon.

However, alongside being terrifying, Minthara is also unexpectedly funny. Her devastating observations aren’t meant to be entertaining, but they often account for some of the funniest dialogue in Baldur’s Gate 3. Ferguson’s restrained delivery would suit these moments perfectly. The biggest challenge in the live-action Baldur’s Gate series would be showing the vulnerability beneath. Fortunately, thanks to roles like Juliette in Silo and Anna in The Girl on the Train, there’s every reason to believe that Rebecca Ferguson could do the subtleties of Minthara just as much justice, allowing moments of intimacy to complicate her character without erasing her more immediate, and troubling, qualities.

'Avengers: Doomsday' Is Making Sure Patrick Stewart Gets a Proper Sendoff

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Patrick Stewart's final on-screen performance will arrive in December's Avengers: Doomsday, and Marvel is making sure the late actor receives a fitting farewell.
  • According to recent reports, marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Anthony and Joe Russo are planning to include a tribute to Stewart in the upcoming superhero blockbuster, according to a new interview with Variety.
  • It has been revealed that the actor had already completed filming for Doomsday, in which he reprises his iconic role as Professor Charles Xavier for the ninth and final time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patrick Stewart's final on-screen performance will arrive in December's Avengers: Doomsday, and Marvel is making sure the late actor receives a fitting farewell.

According to recent reports, marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Anthony and Joe Russo are planning to include a tribute to Stewart in the upcoming superhero blockbuster, according to a new interview with Variety. Stewart died on Oct. 29 at age 86 following a brief battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

It has been revealed that the actor had already completed filming for Doomsday, in which he reprises his iconic role as Professor Charles Xavier for the ninth and final time. Speaking to Variety, Feige revealed that Stewart's last day on set was an emotional occasion, with the actor delivering a speech to the crew.

Recent findings suggest that "He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew," Feige remarked. "We didn't know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.".

Anthony Russo also recalled how difficult filming had become for Stewart as he struggled with his health. Despite the challenges, the actor remained committed to delivering his performance.

"For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional," Russo stated.

Although principal photography has wrapped, Feige said Marvel is now figuring out how to properly honor its longtime collaborator.

In a recent development, "We're long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us," Feige told Variety. "We're looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.".

In a recent development, the tribute will carry particular significance given Stewart's history with the X-Men franchise. He first played Professor X in 2000's X-Men, becoming one of the defining faces of the superhero series alongside Ian McKellen's Magneto. The two actors will reunite in Doomsday, with Joe Russo revealing that their characters share an emotional scene about forgiveness.

"In a lot of ways, Xavier's the conscience in the movie," Russo said. "He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who's his best friend, in the film. It's a very emotional scene about forgiveness, and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing.".

Stewart's death prompted an outpouring of tributes from fans, fellow actors, and gaming communities. Players of No Man's Sky, for example, began naming planets and entire star systems after the actor, with some creating virtual memorials inspired by his portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on Dec. 18.

Latest Update: Cult Hit ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ Returns to Theaters for Major Christmas Expansion

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been four years since the cult hit “Hundreds of Beavers” first debuted and still two years since it started really gaining traction with wider audiences in 2024.
  • Sources indicate that technically, “Hundreds of Beavers” has never left theaters.
  • The re-releases have become a holiday tradition for “Hundreds of Beavers,” which for all its wintery setting and its main character dressed like Santa, is being positioned as a new Christmas movie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been four years since the cult hit “Hundreds of Beavers” first debuted and still two years since it started really gaining traction with wider audiences in 2024. But if it feels like the black and white, silent, slapstick indie comedy still hasn’t left the cultural conversation, that’s because in all that time it has continued to quietly play in theaters and attract audiences both loyal and newly introduced alike.

Sources indicate that technically, “Hundreds of Beavers” has never left theaters. It continues to play individual screenings in a city or two every weekend. Now, though, “Hundreds of Beavers” is set to return to theaters for what is its biggest theatrical expansions to date. The film will kick off its third annual Northwoods Christmas, which will feature 130 screenings across 85 cities, with more to likely be added in the coming weeks. It came about after another fan campaign pushed for the film to come to some markets it hadn’t previously thought about or targeted such as Indianapolis and Charlottesville, and it will now play in everything from concert venues to microcinemas. Related Stories Cinematographer Caleb Deschanel on Finding the Right Techniques For ‘The Right Stuff’ Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

The re-releases have become a holiday tradition for “Hundreds of Beavers,” which for all its wintery setting and its main character dressed like Santa, is being positioned as a new Christmas movie. The first time “Hundreds of Beavers” was re-released at Christmas 2024, which was shortly after the Blu-ray for the film became available, it brought in $118K at the box office in a month, and the producers continued the tradition in 2025.

Industry observers note that “There’s room for a Christmas tradition with the energy of a ‘Rocky Horror’ screening,” noted producer Kurt Ravenwood. “You can watch ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ and ‘White Christmas’ all you want, but for getting together with friends and family to laugh about the miserable winter ahead, ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ has them all beat.”.

Sources indicate that each of the screenings will be preceded by a short film featuring “Bing Crosbeaver,” which they did last year, but this will be a fresh short with a new twist in which another character named “Conspirabeaver” will be joined by a “sinister foe,” per the release. Some of the in-person beavers in costume will be present at the screenings, and fans will also get a promotional poster for the movie. The “Beavers” team recently released a few parody posters ripping off the recent releases of “You Can See Everything,” “Digger,” and “The Devils.”.

It has been revealed that to date, “Hundreds of Beavers” has made $940,092 at the domestic box office, including another $618,014 internationally to bring its worldwide total to above $1.5 million. It’s done all this via first producing the film for just $150,000 and spending little more than $70,000 on ads, publicity, and its many roadshow screenings. It’s also been released entirely independently, starting with a run in the Midwest where the film is set before it started expanding to the coasts.

Incredibly, more than 70 percent of the film’s U.S. box office has come after “Hundreds of Beavers” began streaming way back on April 15, 2024, and it has even sold more than 20,000 Blu-Rays worldwide. It’s a rare, truly indie success story even in a day and age when many movies have pursued self-distribution strategies.

Industry observers note that for those who haven’t had the pleasure of seeing “Hundreds of Beavers” in theaters yet, the film is about a drunken applejack salesman who loses everything and has to survive the winter by becoming North America’s greatest fur trapper. It sees the trapper wrestling and fighting with dozens of beavers and other forest animals all wearing mascot suits, with the stark black and white cinematography and creative physical stunts embracing a zany video game logic and absurd silent comedy slapstick gags.

The film is directed by Mike Cheslik and was written by Cheslik and star Ryland Tews, with the film also starring Olivia Graves, Wes Tank, Doug Mancheski, and Luis Rico.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that DC reveals the identity of Batman's new villain, a dark mirror to Bruce Wayne with even more wealth. Batman pulls off the impossible feat of maintaining his status as a Gotham billionaire socialite while operating nightly as the Dark Knight. By day, Bruce plays the charming if slightly reckless playboy philanthropist, hosting charity galas and staging harmless public distractions that convince Gotham’s media and criminal underworld he's far too pampered and scatterbrained to ever be Batman. Behind closed doors, his strict time management and trusted allies keep Wayne Enterprises running smoothly while Bruce puts on the Batsuit to fight crime.

Gotham City’s upper crust overflows with equally wealthy and influential elites who use their fortunes for less honorable purposes. Oswald Cobblepot runs a huge financial and criminal empire from the Iceberg Lounge, Roman Sionis inherited Janus Cosmetics before building a ruthless mob syndicate, and Thomas Elliot twisted his privileged upbringing into a bitter vendetta against Bruce Wayne himself. Elsewhere in Gotham’s high society, the Court of Owls manipulates the city’s economy from opulent hidden parlors, while Ferris Boyle exploits his monopoly at the expense of innocent lives.

Batman's rogues' gallery hasn't stopped growing, and that includes rival millionaires who weaponize their wealth and influence to oppose Bruce Wayne's heroic efforts.

One full year since his introduction, DC pulls back the curtain on the mysterious mastermind who has restructured Gotham’s underworld since Batman #1. Beneath the minimalist robotic bull mask and dapper three-piece suit, the Minotaur is actually a man named "Max," whose unmasked face and true name are revealed as Batman 2026 Annual #1 takes readers straight to the center of the Torus conspiracy. Max openly declares that his real superpower is cash. He weaponizes capital and banking control to bend the city's deadliest criminals to his will.

According to recent reports, the Minotaur's unapologetically wealth-centered philosophy sets him apart from theatrical Gotham villains, who are more commonly associated with tragic accidents, scientific experiments, or gimmicky crime enterprises. Most importantly, it frames Max as a dark mirror to Bruce Wayne himself. Without superhuman abilities, Max treats organized crime like a business as he maps out plans to take a cut of every legitimate and illicit revenue stream in Gotham within twenty months. Alongside Jesse Lonergan’s companion backup, which reveals the Calculator is secretly manipulating Max's "algorithm of crime" for his own ends, Batman 2026 Annual #1 cements the Minotaur as a grounded threat with a bottomless bankroll that rivals Batman's own.

Recent findings suggest that very few Batman villains have achieved lasting household-name status alongside icons like the Joker, Two-Face, or the Riddler in the past two decades. Professor Pyg earned genuine cult acclaim through Grant Morrison’s Batman and Robin and later video game and television appearances, and The Batman Who Laughs became ubiquitous largely through an aggressive push from DC Comics across multiple multiverse crossovers. Meanwhile, modern Gotham creations like the Designer, Failsafe, Ghost-Maker, and Punchline have struggled to maintain permanent relevance once their original arcs and writers moved on.

The Bronze Age of the 1970s delivered Ra’s al Ghul, Talia al Ghul, and Man-Bat in rapid succession, and the early 1990s explosion of Bane, Harley Quinn, and Victor Zsasz prove it's possible for Batman to get villains that last. For the Minotaur to avoid fading into obscurity after Matt Fraction's Torus saga wraps up, future writers will need to lean into what makes him genuinely different from traditional costumed criminals. Max's ruthless "cash as a superpower" philosophy and his role as a white-collar crime lord who can bankroll or bankrupt Gotham's classic underworld are his best assets, but he may also need to showcase a wider variety of attributes to stay around longer.

What do you think about the Minotaur?

Batman 2026 Annual #1 is now available from DC Comics.
