📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

IndieWire, the definitive outlet for creative independence in film and TV, unveiled on Wednesday, November 25 the final additions to the lineup for the Winter 2026 edition of our IndieWire Honors event, featuring our largest lineup yet of film honorees. Curated and selected by IndieWire’s editorial team, IndieWire Honors is a celebration of the filmmakers, actors, and artisans key to crafting some of the most exciting cinematic works this year.

In a recent development, the newly announced honorees include “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and costume designer Trish Summerville, who will be receiving the Spotlight Award. They join previously announced honorees John Turturro, Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield, Ike Barinholtz, Yura Borisov, James Gray, Adam Driver, Beth de Araújo, Mason Reeves, Gemma Chan, Ruth Madeley, David Greaves, Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo, Jeon Do-yeon, Anthony Ippolito, James Ortiz, Neal Scanlan, Mag Sarnowska, Paul Lambert, and Travis Knight. Related Stories Cult Hit ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ Returns to Theaters for Big Christmas Expansion Cinematographer Caleb Deschanel on Finding the Right Techniques For ‘The Right Stuff’.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, IndieWire has announced that the incoming awards ceremony will be hosted by writer and comedian Demi Adejuyigbe, whose latest special “Demi Adejuyigbe Is Going to Do 1 (One) Backflip” is now available to stream on Dropout. Previous IndieWire Honors emcees include Emmy winner Alex Edelman, Emmy nominee Robby Hoffman, multi-hyphenate Dewayne Perkins, and lauded comedians Vinny Thomas and Atsuko Okatsuka.

IndieWire Honors will take place on Thursday, December 3 in Los Angeles, starting with an intimate cocktail reception and awards ceremony. IndieWire will also begin rolling out exclusive editorial content, including honoree profiles, on Friday, November 27 through the lead-up to the awards night. Throughout the ceremony, into the next day, IndieWire will publish photos and exclusive social content from the event as well. The ceremony’s host will be announced at a later date.

“It’s thrilling to be able to recognize the artists behind so many of this year’s most exciting and compelling films,” noted Brent Lang, IndieWire’s editor-in-chief. “They dazzled us with their talent, inspired us with their willingness to take risks, and left an indelible mark on cinema. We are excited to celebrate their accomplishments.”.

“It’s exciting to celebrate such an eclectic group of film talent for this year’s IndieWire Honors,” stated James Israel, IndieWire’s SVP and Publisher. “We are also pleased to continue to celebrate top craft artisans in entertainment.”.

The Winter 2026 IndieWire Honors honorees are:.

In a recent development, the fact that he is known for being a frequent collaborator of both Spike Lee and the Coen brothers conveys just how expansive an actor Turturro is. The Brooklyn native is quintessentially Latest York, as most recently proven in Sony Pictures Classics’ acclaimed Sundance premiere “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” written and directed by Noah Segan. Yet, a filmmaker can still drop the performer into the corporate dystopia of sci-fi series “Severance,” or have him go on a Southern odyssey in “O Brother, Where Art Thou?,” and he just as well hits it out of the park.

With nearly five decades of film work under his belt, starting with an uncredited role in “Raging Bull,” Turturro manages to be one of the few veteran actors who continues to best himself year after year.

It has been revealed that the pair of Madrid-based directors colloquially known as Los Javis are not shy about cluing the audience in on the shoulders upon which they stand on. They cast Penélope Cruz and Lola Dueñas, two muses of auteur Pedro Almodóvar, as the most crucial women within their epic adaptation of an unfinished play by Federico García Lorca, another one of Spain’s queer artist forefathers. That reverence is balanced by the confidence in their own eye for fresh talent, weaving together three different timelines led by three relative unknowns, including most notably, indie musician Guitarricadelafuente, who also contributed the poignant original song “La Nieve” to the project.

Industry observers note that made outside the Hollywood system and chosen to represent Spain in the Best International Feature Oscar race, the Netflix release “La Bola Negra” is a film of immense scale. If viewers knew nothing of the director duo before seeing the film, they come away with a crash course in everything they are about. Considering how they won both the Best Director Award at Cannes, and the coveted People’s Choice Award at TIFF, it seems to be an experience most cinephiles enjoy.

In a recent development, “Tallgrass” is the code word that unlocks what makes the creative collaboration between “Paper Tiger” writer-director James Gray and star Adam Driver such a feat. Though the Neon release, which premiered at Cannes, is their first time ever working together, the filmmaker imbues the two-time Oscar nominee with such a specific vision of what it feels like to realize one’s time has gone by. Though the film is another deeply personal work in the oeuvre of the Queens-born auteur, Driver adds a more broad portrait of a figure wrapped up in crime, slowly feeling the overwhelming situation constrict and constrict.

“Josephine” was not made to be an easy watch, but boasts the rare feat of winning both the Grand Jury Prize and Audience Award at the Sundance Film Festival. Written and directed by Araújo, and starring Gemma Chan and Mason Reeves as mother and daughter, the drama is a bold exploration of how little control parents have over their children being confronted by certain horrors in life that there’s no guarantee of avoiding.

In a recent development, an early release for fresh distributor Sumerian Pictures, “Josephine” has only felt more necessary as the year has gone on, and news stories like the Cornell rape case have come to the forefront. It is a conversation piece about a subject many wish to evade, that puts forth the effort to reach meaningful discourse.

Sources indicate that the most bold artistic choice in “Artificial,” the latest film from prolific director Luca Guadagnino, is to not proffer any romance in becoming one of the Promethean figures. The repeated refrain of “Feel the AGI” rings as a benevolent threat by the time the two hours and 20 minutes of the Neon release are over. Garfield, Borisov, Barbaro, and Barinholtz, all four playing key figures in the genesis of OpenAI, play incredibly off of each other as tech titans forcing a smile as they convince their audience artificial technology is inevitable. Join or die. Their joint efforts to invoke a common sense of humanity would be funny if the reality of the situation weren’t so uncanny.

Recent findings suggest that re-teaming with her “Secret Sunshine” director Lee Chang-dong almost 20 years later, the “Possible Love” star is unmissable as a woman caught in a class divide between her blue collar, out-of-work husband, and the couple that hosts them as a means to interview them for a documentary. It is a role that she said uses “the whole entirety of her body” to push back against the weight of capitalism. The Netflix film chosen to represent South Korea in the Best International Feature category at the 2027 Oscars offers a feast of ideas, with Jeon’s layered turn as Mi-ok alone being enough fodder for many conversations to come.

It has been revealed that all sorts of biopics enter theaters each year, but few task their leads with the difficult job of playing someone still actively in the public eye. In Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky,” from Amazon MGM Studios, newcomer Ippolito deftly captures the distinctive look and sound of a young and hungry Sylvester Stallone. But what is more impressive than that form of transformation is how the 27-year-old actor captures the spirit of the unlikely star and scribe of the 1977 Best Picture winner. How some of his best moments come when he himself plays Rocky is a meta element we are still unpacking, but add it to the overwhelming evidence that Ippolito is one to watch.

There is a standout moment in Oscar winner Siân Heder’s “Being Heumann” in which Madeley, as trailblazing disability rights activist Judy Heumann, asks a well-meaning congressman what he means by calling her “inspiring.” “Inspired to do what?,” she says. It is a moment that clarifies that the film about Heumann leading the successful protest to get the government to sign Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act is not standard fare about a woman in a wheelchair overcoming odds, but a film about her refusing to let those odds overcome her.

Madeley embodies a fight against circumstances that applies to more than just the disability community. May casting directors take notice of the limitless potential she offers as part of any type of ensemble.

It has been revealed that as the President and CEO of Laika Studios, Knight has spent over 20 years educating audiences on the artform of stop-motion animation. And still, in his latest film “Wildwood,” a fantasy epic taking place in the forests outside Portland, Oregon, Knight directs scenes that seem inexplicable. It is hard enough to animate one bird flying, using that technique, yet the Fathom Entertainment release sees whole flocks fly off toward a war between species. The film’s commentary on parents and children is as heartrending as the craft behind how the film was made is genuinely inspiring to filmmakers of all types.

Talk about legacy. Decades after his father, noted documentarian William Greaves, hosted a party for the surviving members of the Harlem Renaissance, “Once Upon a Time in Harlem” co-directed finished the film, one of the gems of Sundance 2026. To listen to Black luminaries from the ‘20s speak about how their work has endured into the ‘70s, with the dramatic irony of watching the film through a modern lens, is a singular cinematic experience. In a year where there is so much conversation around what pushes the documentary artform forward, the Neon release delivers both necessary context and innovation.

There is humor in having puppetry, one of the world’s oldest artforms, at the center of a conversation around innovation, but come on. Ortiz’s performance as Rocky in “Project Hail Mary,” supported by the work of visual effects team leaders Scanlan, Lambert, and Sarnowska, made us fall in love with a spidery alien rock that has no mouth or face. Puppetry’s forebearers would have still found that to be an insurmountable challenge. Hence, why the artist behind the fan favorite character opposite Ryan Gosling in the Amazon MGM Studios blockbuster deserves their flowers for helping viewers go beyond their earthly imaginations.

Though the latest film from director David Fincher and screenwriter Quentin Tarantino furthers the mis-adventures of Cliff Booth, the role that earned star Brad Pitt an Oscar, the Netflix film has an identity all its own. The work of costume designer Trish Summerville and actor Yahya Abdul-Mateen II are two elements that put that into focus, really easing the audience into the jump forward to 1977, where the silks flowed, and fur dripped off fresh screen icons akin to the latter’s Rodrick “Hot Rod” Harrison. This go-round allows viewers to have an appreciation for more than just Hollywood, but the greater Los Angeles area, and all the distinct styles it brought in that pivotal ‘70s moment.

There's nothing quite like hearing "Your call is notable to us" for the 15th time while trying to track down a missing holiday package. And apparently, I'm not alone in my frustration.

A newly introduced survey from voice AI company PolyAI found that 69.4% of respondents would be willing to speak with an AI voice assistant instead of waiting for a human customer service representative if they were guaranteed zero wait time.

The survey of 1,087 U.S. consumers, conducted in November 2026, suggests that despite reservations about AI replacing human workers, many Americans are open to the technology when it solves an everyday problem.

With Black Friday deals already underway and Cyber Monday just days away, AI could offer some relief from one of the biggest headaches of holiday shopping.

According to the survey shared with Tom's Guide, nearly 68% of respondents say automated phone menus frequently or almost always fail to resolve their problems no matter how much customers try to get around them. Just one in four consumers reports having their problem resolved on the first call.

Recent findings suggest that poor customer service is also affecting where people shop. Some 64.4% of respondents have abandoned a holiday purchase or canceled an order because of a bad customer service experience.

Perhaps the most entertaining findings from the survey are what people would rather do than navigate an automated phone menu:.

In a recent development, while Gen Z is often associated with AI adoption, millennials were the most receptive to AI-powered customer service in this survey. More than 75% stated they would use a voice AI assistant if it meant eliminating wait times.

Perhaps more surprising is that 62% of baby boomers and older respondents noted they would do the same.

Industry observers note that however, consumers aren't necessarily ready to give up human customer service entirely. Nearly 68% of respondents noted they would feel comfortable using voice AI if they could be transferred to a human representative when necessary.

Shoppers surveyed also wanted AI to do more than answer basic questions. They were interested in assistants that could tell them whether something was in stock, solve a problem without asking for the same information twice or text them a receipt or boarding pass before they hung up.

Of course, there's a major difference between an AI assistant that sounds human and one that can actually get things done. Much of that comes down to how well a firm has integrated AI into its existing customer service systems.

We've all been stuck on a customer service call, pressing buttons and repeating ourselves just to get through to someone who can help. Conversational AI promises to make that experience a little less painful.

Instead of sitting through a lengthy phone menu, you could simply explain that your package was delivered to the wrong house or that you need to change your flight, much like you would with a human agent. What do you think about AI customer service? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple.
  • Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….
  • It has been revealed that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the manufacturer’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….

It has been revealed that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

Industry observers note that it’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.).

Recent findings suggest that I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, owners should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy users at least would like a little more transparency and control.

In a recent development, airPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant patch in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, owners had to wait until it “just worked.”.

According to recent reports, apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an revision, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

According to recent reports, make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

According to recent reports, another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It has been revealed that it’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

Sources indicate that will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

In a recent development, once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

Recent findings suggest that I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that right now happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

According to recent reports, is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cats make a wonderful household pet, but cleaning their litter box is not so much fun, which is why I’ve tried several automatic litter boxes over the years to see if any could make it less of a chore.

According to recent reports, the latest model I’ve been using, the Homerunpet Self Cleaning Cat Litter Box Kit, is the most expensive, and largest one I’ve yet brought into my house. I — or more specifically my cats — have been using it for about two months, and they seem to have taken to it well. However, before you spend upwards of $600 on this thing, there’s a few things you should know first.

This self-cleaning litter box is designed for cats up to 25 pounds, works with a variety of litter, a 12L waste bin with odor control, and has an app that lets you monitor your cats' weight.

This litterbox is huge. The box it came in was larger than ones I got with microwaves. Measuring 23.62 x 28.07 x 27.44 inches, you’re definitely going to need a lot of space for it, so I would not recommend it if you’re planning to put it in a smallish bathroom.

The HomeRun Pet litterbox looks kind of like a cement mixer. The main part of the box is a large drum with a hole in its side; this is where your cat enters and does its business. When they’re done, and after a minute or two, the litterbox rotates this section to empty the waste into a small storage bin on the side, and then refreshes the clean litter from a reservoir.

To the right of this main drum is a reservoir into which you pour fresh litter. The machine will draw from this reservoir to replenish the main tray.

No more scooping! When the machine empties itself, waste is funneled into a small bin on the right side, which you line with an included plastic bag. When the bag is full — you'll get an alert on your phone — you simply pull the bin out and remove the bag. Replacement bags cost $35 for a pack of 60. With two cats, we’ve had to replace the bag once every two weeks or so.

In a recent development, there’s actually two trays; a second one, which sits directly below the drum, can be used if you want to completely empty the litter box. And, every piece of the litter box that could possibly get dirty can be removed and washed.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

This being a “smart” cat litter box, you get all sorts of updates via the HomeRun app — when it needs to be emptied, when you need to add upcoming litter, how long your cats take, and how many times they go per day.

One interesting feature of the HomeRun Pet is that it has a built-in scale, so you can keep tabs on your cats’ weight. I initially had to wait until each of mine used the box to figure out which was which, but after that, it would tell me which cat had gone, and when. Of course, if your cats are very close in weight, it might have trouble telling the difference. If that’s the case, you can adjust the weight error value, so it can better distinguish between multiple pets.

The app also lets you customize all sorts of things, like the type of litter you’re using, cleaning schedule, and even “kitten protection,” to prevent the device from activating automatically.

Recent findings suggest that in order to use the HomeRun, your cat has to step up about a foot to get inside the opening; knowing how a cat of mine had trouble walking in his later years, I highly doubt he’d have been able to make it up. Something like the PetSafe Smart Self-Cleaning Litterbox would make more sense (and it’s a lot cheaper and takes up a lot less space).

Industry observers note that the Homerunpet Self Cleaning Cat Litter Box Kit is not a small investment; even with Black Friday sales, you’re still going to spend $659 at Amazon on this thing. And, it takes up a lot of space. However, it does make cleaning up after your cat incredibly convenient - just slide open a tray, remove a bag, and you’re all set. Is that worth the price of a nice TV? That’s for you to decide.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Warning: contains spoilers for Justice League Unlimited #25!
  • It has been revealed that DC has confirmed the return of a major Snyderverse Justice League villain, nine years after their last appearance.
  • The Snyderverse debuted in 2013 with the arrival of The Man of Steel in theaters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: contains spoilers for Justice League Unlimited #25!

It has been revealed that DC has confirmed the return of a major Snyderverse Justice League villain, nine years after their last appearance. The DCEU, or “the Snyderverse” as some called it, was DC’s first serious attempt at a cohesive cinematic universe, similar to the MCU. Snyderverse DC films were released consistently for nearly a decade, before the powers that be placed James Gunn in charge.

The Snyderverse debuted in 2013 with the arrival of The Man of Steel in theaters. Starring Henry Cavill as Superman, Amy Adams as Lois Lane and Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, the film was a hit with audiences, but not critics or devoted fans. A follow-up, Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice, hit the screens in 2016. Starring Ben Affleck as The Dark Knight, the film seeded the Justice League, introducing Wonder Woman, the Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg to the mix. Like its predecessor, Dawn of Justice received mixed reviews.

Recent findings suggest that during the filming of Justice League, Snyder stepped down from directorial duties due to a family tragedy. Snyder’s involvement with the DCEU faded, leading to films that, while good and entertaining, failed to connect with audiences in the same fashion that Marvel’s movies did. The Snyderverse ended with The Flash, which reset the timeline. Vocal segments of the fandom have demanded Snyder’s vision be reinstated, but the possibility of that happening fades over time. Now, those yearning for a return to the Snyderverse are in luck, as one of its biggest villains returns.

Steppenwolf was created by Jack Kirby, and first appeared in 1972's Latest Gods #7.

In Justice League Unlimited #25, written by Mark Waid and drawn by Dan Mora, Plastic Man and Detective Chimp are horrified to discover that Steppenwolf, Darkseid’s uncle and a major threat in his own right, has set up a weapons forge underneath the Galaxy Communications Building in Metropolis. They look on as swarms of Parademons put together fantastic weapons for Steppenwolf to use in the service of Darkseid.

According to recent reports, the gravity of the League’s situation begins to set in, and Plastic Man starts to panic. The two heroes then learn that Maxwell Lord, wearing the sign of Darkseid on his forehead, is offering support to Steppenwolf and his hordes. Before the two can escape to warn the Justice League, they are taken out by Kanto the Assassin.

Darkseid has many zealots and henchmen waiting to do his bidding, such as Desaad, Mantis and Granny Goodness. Nearly all of Darkseid’s family is at his beck and call too, such as his children Kalibak and Grail, as well as Steppenwolf. One of the most feared warriors in the galaxy, Steppenwolf is powerful enough to take Doomsday down to the wire. On top of being a formidable combatant, Steppenwolfe also has his legions of Parademons, whose only desire is to obey and kill for Darkseid.

Movie goers will remember Steppenwolf from 2017’s Justice League movie, where he served as one of the film’s antagonists. Played by Ciaran Hinds, Steppenwolfe attacked Atlantis and Themyscira and took their Mother Boxes. Steppenwolfe planned to enslave Earth’s population, but the combined efforts of the Justice League were able to stop him. Steppenwolf is one of DC’s most underrated villains, but Justice League failed him. When Snyder finally released his cut in 2021, Steppenwolf’s role was larger, allowing audiences to get to know him better, and fear him appropriately.

Steppenwolf is one of DC’s most underrated villains, but Justice League failed him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A posh, Philippine country club’s colonial secrets are exposed in Rafael Manuel’s evocatively creepy, grimly funny, and austerely constructed social satire, “Filipiñana,” set outside Manila.

Industry observers note that writer/director Rafael Manuel’s film, which won a World Cinema special jury award at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, also stands a chance at being his country’s first representative on a Best International Feature Film Oscar shortlist. While the Philippines was among the eight countries that submitted during the category’s inaugural year in 1956 (with Lamberto V. Avellana’s “Child of Sorrow”) along with France, Italy, and others, it’s never been nominated or shortlisted. Related Stories IndieWire Honors Film Celebration to Fête John Turturro, the ‘Artificial’ Cast, Los Javis, and More Cult Hit ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ Returns to Theaters for Significant Christmas Expansion.

Executive-produced by Manuel’s former mentor Jia Zhangke, “Filipiñana” follows a tee girl who discovers something is off (and downright sinister) about the club’s administration, specifically president Dr. Palanca (Teroy Guzman). She’s played by Jorrybell Agoto, who, at just 32 years old, died earlier in November after a short battle with lymphoma.

IndieWire’s interview with filmmaker Rafael Manuel took place a week before the news, though he shared in a later statement, “The tragedy of this loss cannot be put into words. The world has just lost one of its brightest stars. We have just lost a great friend. But our thoughts and prayers go out especially to Jorybell’s family, who have just lost a loving ate [the Filipino word for older sister] and a devoted daughter.”.

An elegaic air, too, hangs over the film in retrospect and even before Agoto’s passing, as “Filipiñana” dwells in ghosts of the Philippines’ imperial past and Spanish occupation.

Sources indicate that “No one explains it to you beforehand,” director Manuel told IndieWire of touring with his first feature for nearly a year. (We spoke over Zoom while he smoked a cigarette in his Amsterdam apartment.) “What I’m starting to realize is the biggest difference between short and feature is that with short festival, it’s kind of the end goal. When you premiere at your festival, you’re so happy, and it’s done; it’s like people get to see it finally. But with a feature film, it’s just the beginning, and no one explained this to me.”.

Manuel joins the ranks of Lav Diaz, Brillante Mendoza, the late Lino Brocka, and many others to represent the Philippines at the Academy Awards — a concept, he noted, that was never really on his radar.

Industry observers note that “When we were coming up with this film and the genesis of the film, you don’t really think about an Oscars race,” stated Manuel. “You just think about making the best film you can. And especially coming from Southeast Asia, access to the American market, even getting a U.S. theatrical release, it’s not something that’s very common. Usually, your usual route is via the European arthouse market. So it’s been really surprising and in the best way possible, seeing how well received the film is in the States, in North America, and in the Anglo world in general.”.

The process was a “very challenging one,” he said, as the Philippines is taking the Oscar push very seriously from a governmental perspective. “And to be the first film that’s seriously backed by the government means a lot to us,” he said, especially for a film that’s critical of government and social hierarchy.

And there are hat tips not only to Jacques Tati, but also to Wes Anderson and Michael Haneke, at least in reviews, in terms of the movie’s flattened remove from violence and its dryly observational approach where everything in the frame is meticulously arranged.

Industry observers note that “I get why people are saying Michael Haneke and Wes Anderson,” he said. “I mean, Jacques Tati, obviously, he’s a really massive influence for me, but for example, with Haneke, I feel like we tackle violence very differently from how Haneke tackles violence. And I think with Wes Anderson, I see it because of the colors, because of the symmetrical framing and all of that, but I think this is very much a satire of that. And so, yes, we use a lot of Western codes and Western aesthetics in the film, but because it’s a film that deals with Western influence in the Orient, it was a film that deals with colonization. So the form and the aesthetic of the film is very much part of the satire. It’s the form.”.

He added, “It’s a polarizing film. I think it’s either you love it or you hate it, and I think that’s the same whether you’re in the West or in the Philippines.”.

The distribution of world cinema in the Philippines also helps to explain the divided palate for “Filipiñana,” as audiences have very little exposure to arthouse cinema from the outside world.

“In the Philippines, distribution of world cinema, it’s almost nonexistent. In Metro Manila, we have basically one or two arthouse cinemas, independent cinemas. The rest of the cinemas are all in shopping malls, and all they play are local rom-coms or Marvel movies,” he remarked. But challenges in the West of audience fatigue over shopworn, recycled I.P. and familiar material also apply in the Philippines.

In a recent development, “It’s been a hot topic lately in the Philippines and consumers and audiences complaining about formulaic Filipino filmmaking. They’re tired of the formulaic rom-coms. But then the thing is that in the Philippines, I would say 90 percent of people have never seen a Lav Diaz film, even maybe 99 percent of people haven’t seen a Lav Diaz film,” Manuel mentioned of the slow cinema master behind last year’s submission, the Gael García Bernal-starring “Magellan,” which also dealt in the Philippines’ colonized history. (Diaz and Manuel share producers, including Bianca Balbuena and Bradley Liew, though they’ve never actually met.).

“Filipiñana” marks a break from tradition in terms of its Westernized style — and chatter has been flying on Letterboxd over the film since the Sundance premiere. (“I look through Letterboxd sometimes. Well, I used to, I stopped. And then the unhealthy thing with Letterboxd, for me especially, is that I’ll skip all the good comments and I’ll just read all the bad comments,” he noted.).

“When you’re faced with something different with arthouse cinema, like Filipino arthouse cinema, when Filipino audiences are faced with Filipino arthouse cinema, and you get some violent reactions, then it begs the question, ‘When you’re complaining about being tired of formulaic Filipino filmmaking, what exactly do you mean, and what exactly is it that you want?’ Do you just want Hollywood films but with brown faces in them? Because I don’t think that’s the answer either.”.

“Filipiñana” is now streaming on Kino Film Collection.

#108634. 'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (821 w)

'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home.
  • While the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home users might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks.
  • Recent findings suggest that wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home. "Wifi motion sensing" turns your ISP’s router into a motion detector, letting providers know exactly how many people are in the house, where they are situated, individual movement patterns, and, in some cases, even body shapes that could approximate a person’s identity.

While the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home users might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks. So here’s how wifi routers sense motion, what they can do with it, who has access to the data, and how you can disable it.

Recent findings suggest that wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances. Those same radio signals are also absorbed and reflected by the human body as they travel in all directions from the router. With the right software, ISPs can track how those wifi signals travel around your room, which can be studied to detect presence and sense motion patterns.

As long as your ISP’s router model supports this feature natively, it doesn’t require any additional hardware to be installed in your home. For example, Xfinity’s version of the feature pairs your router with five other connected appliances in your room to create oval-shaped sensing zones that can track your presence and movement within those spaces.

Sources indicate that it isn’t a new feature, either—companies like Cognitive Systems and Origin Wireless that supply networking hardware to ISPs have been offering wifi motion sensing for years now, while early research prototypes from the MIT date back at least as far as 2015. In 2025, IEEE updated its Wi-Fi 802.11 standard to include motion sensing and lay out the architectural guidelines for it, which makes it likely that even more routers will now ship with the feature.

In its current consumer form, wifi motion sensing can help you control smart home apparatus like lights or thermostats, get pet safety notifications on your phone, set up a fall alert system for elderly customers, and trigger appliances remotely based on human presence. But enabling it carries risks.

Most providers, including Cognitive Systems, claim that the technology isn’t sensitive to identity and can’t be used to track specific individuals. But even if true, that’s more likely to be a product decision rather than a technical limitation. Karlsruhe Institute researchers have shown that even ordinary wifi signals can identify individuals with a 99.5% accuracy.

It has been revealed that also worth noting: ISPs’ legal wording suggests that they may disclose the collected and stored motion data at any time to law enforcement, government agencies, regulators, and courts in response to subpoenas or during an emergency. ISPs may also retain your motion data in the cloud long-term in case they are required to facilitate a subpoena in the future.

As far as major ISPs are concerned, Xfinity (Comcast) is the only broadband provider that currently offers this feature across its commercial routers on the XB7, XB8, XB9, XB10, MXB1, and XER10 gateways. It’s opted out by default, but in case you or a family member already switched it on, you can disable it again by navigating to Home > WiFi Motion on the Xfinity app, click on the gear icon on the live view page, and tap Remove WiFi Motion.

Verizon Fios customers also had access to a Home Awareness feature on their routers that could be toggled on or off using the MyFios app, but that’s since been discontinued. In an official disclosure published shortly after the discontinuation, Verizon notified customers that it has deleted all associated movement logs from this service and no longer retains any motion data from consumers.

But there are other regional ISPs that offer it, too. For example, Breezeline (Atlantic Broadband) offers a feature called Motion within its Plume-powered application that alerts customers when movement is detected in their homes, among its other features. MidCo, a telecom tech giant in the Upper Midwest, has a feature called Sense which can be toggled on or off using the MidCo Wi-Fi app. Plume, ADT-owned Origin Wireless, and Airties—all of whom supply technology to ISPs—have also been marketing motion sensing to customers for the last few years.

Sources indicate that if you’re unsure if your wifi router or ISP has motion sensing features or opts you in by default, look for a feature called “Sense,” “Motion,” or equivalent in your broadband’s mobile app. Exact steps differ greatly from one ISP to another, so it’s best not to assume that they will all opt you out by default, or that they collect the same types of data. With the 802.11bf patch to IEEE standards in 2025, this technology will be accessible to even more router manufacturers, so expect adoption to grow among internet providers as well.

  • “To make them look real, talking about practical and how important that is, I from Day One felt like you had to base these characters on real sheep,” Page stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s not every day you see a movie where talking sheep get to be the stars. But Kyle Balda’s “The Sheep Detectives” does exactly that. The Amazon MGM film flips the whodunnit formula on its head with a barnyard murder mystery in which a group of sheep have to solve the murder of their beloved shepherd. Much of the film’s success can be attributed to the juxtaposition between a whimsical plot and the realism with which it’s executed. The sheep might talk and solve crimes, but they look like real animals you’d find on any farm.

During the VFX section of IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, “The Sheep Detectives” Visual Effects Supervisor Graham Page broke down the meticulous research process that made the sheep look so lifelike. Related Stories ‘Filipiñana’ Could Be the Philippines’ First-Ever Oscar-Shortlisted Feature — Even as the Film Was Dealt an Unexpected Tragedy IndieWire Honors Film Celebration to Fête John Turturro, the ‘Artificial’ Cast, Los Javis, and More.

“To make them look real, talking about practical and how important that is, I from Day One felt like you had to base these characters on real sheep,” Page stated. “We filmed [real sheep] with multiple cameras and getting on boxes. We had a script, almost, like ‘These are the things the sheep need to do in the film.’ Even before an animator can touch it, another artist modeled the skeleton and the muscle and fat. And then you have a rigger and a facial artist, all of these artists.”.

He went on to explain how that research process produced character-defining details that they would not have discovered any other way.

It has been revealed that “We started to come up with what we would call ‘Sheep-isms’ that help kind of bring some of that natural movement,” he noted. “There’s a little ear twitch. And a human can’t twitch their ear, but it felt so right. We were like ‘This is really nice,’ and it emphasized the character and the story and the emotion. But it was brought out of a sheep.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, popular secure messaging app Signal has rolled out a fresh patch that automatically disables screenshots for the sake of blocking Siri AI from reading your chats. Here are the details.

Signal’s latest app enhancement on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t right now provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.

By default, people who upgrade and try to take a screenshot will see a message that says: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”.

It has been revealed that fortunately, there’s an easy workaround. Customers who want to re-enable screenshots can do so by visiting Signal’s privacy settings and turning off the latest toggle that’s labeled ‘Block Siri AI.’.

Here’s 9to5Mac’s own Arin Waichulis:.

Signal now blocks in-app screenshots on iPhone to keep Siri AI from reading chatsIt’s a newly introduced toggle in settings that’s on by default, but can be turned offNo equivalent for its Mac app pic.twitter.com/ImsinqMNPq.

Here’s exactly what that toggle does, per the in-app settings:.

According to recent reports, prevent Siri AI from scanning Signal content. This will also block you from taking screenshots in the app and App Switcher.

According to recent reports, it’s good to see that users can manually disable the fresh privacy setting if they want. But Signal’s decision to block screenshots does raise important questions about the potential gap in privacy tools for iOS developers.

Recent findings suggest that apple already lets you block Siri AI from accessing whichever apps you manually exclude, and that became even easier in iOS 27.2. But rather than directing people to that system option, Signal seems to believe it needed to take action itself with this patch.

#108629. 10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1302 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1302 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone.
  • This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually.
  • There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone. Over the past year, Google has consistently added features to manage your belongings, share your location with loved ones, and locate lost devices. Find Hub can now notify you when you've left your device or your tracker behind. Plus, you can use Gemini to remember where you left items, even without a tracker attached. Behind the scenes, there are even more hidden settings and features to help track your devices and make it easier to retrieve them in case they are stolen or misplaced. If you use Find Hub, you need to know about these 10 hacks.

This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually. AirTags customers should be familiar with this feature already. When you leave your tracker or device behind, and exit the location range, you’ll receive a notification that you left without your item. You need to enable this feature on a per-device basis. Go to Find Hub and select a device. Tap the settings gear icon next to the device's name, and enable Notify when left behind. While you’re here, go to Add location to add familiar locations where you don’t want to get a notification (like your home or workspace). Otherwise, Find Hub may spam you with left behind alerts.

There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker. You can simply ask Gemini to remember where you put things, and it will show up in the Find Hub app. To use it, pull up Gemini and say something like, “Remember in Find Hub that the passport is in the downstairs wardrobe,” or “I’ve kept the spare car keys behind the garage door.”.

It has been revealed that you can then ask Gemini, “Where did I keep my passport?” and it will tell you. If you change the location of an item, just ask Gemini to patch it for you. When you go to the Remembered tab, you’ll see the location of all remembered items. You can also add items manually here using the Add button.

Some Android smartphones can remain findable for several hours after they've been switched off or their batteries have run out. If you’re using a supported device (like the latest Pixel series smartphone), you can use a hardware feature to track the location using Google’s mesh network, relying on nearby devices (similar to how Android tags work).

It has been revealed that to make sure this feature is enabled, go to Find Hub, and tap Find your offline devices. Here, make sure that either With network in busy places only or With network everywhere is selected.

According to recent reports, if you’re using a tracker in your car, luggage, or on your keys, you might want to share location access with your spouse or family members. Find Hub has a feature called "Share Ownership" that lets you share the tracker details with up to 10 people. Only the location of your tracker is shared, not your personal device.

To set it up, go to Find Hub, and choose the tracker or accessory that you want to share. Tap the Share Ownership button and follow the on-screen instructions to share the invite link via a messaging app or using Quick Share. Once the recipient taps Accept, you’ll get a notification. Go to the device settings in Find Hub and tap the Confirm button to enable location sharing.

Sources indicate that you can quickly share your live location with your friends or loved ones using Google Messages. Open a conversation, tap the Attachment icon, and choose Real-time location. Set the duration and tap Send.

If you don’t like using the Messages app, you can do so directly from Find Hub. Go to the People tab at the bottom of the screen, and tap the Plus icon. Choose the duration and select a contact to share the location with, then tap the Get Link button to copy the link. You can then share it via any messaging app of your choice.

Recent findings suggest that you might have a Find Hub tracker in your luggage to help keep tabs on your bags. But you don't have to be the only one privy to its location. If your airline loses that luggage, you can temporarily share its location with your airline to help you retrieve it. This is an official feature, too: Google partnered with multiple airlines to make this data sharing easier. From the Find Hub, choose your tracker. Tap the Share Item Location button, and then tap Share Item Location again. Copy the generated web link and share it with your airline using the app or support page. The link will automatically expire in seven days, so you don't have to worry about your airline continuing to monitor your luggage's location long after your flight.

Find Hub uses a mesh network of supported Android devices to securely locate your lost device or tag. But by default, it waits until multiple Android devices detect the location of the lost device. This works well if you've lost the device in crowded areas, but it can increase your wait time if you lose it somewhere remote. Luckily, there is a hidden setting that triggers location sharing even if a single device reports its location. Go to Settings > Google > All services > Find Hub > Find your offline devices and select With network everywhere instead of With network in busy places only.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve lost your smartphone, you don’t need to rush to a computer or a website to track it. Borrow someone’s Android smartphone and head into their Find Hub. Tap Sign in as guest and sign in with your Google account associated with your device, then find and select your device in the account. If requested, enter the PIN that you’ve previously set up. You can now track the device’s location, get directions to the device, or play a sound to help track the device if it’s nearby. If the device is truly lost, you can use the Mark as Lost feature to remotely lock your device.

In a recent development, map-based tracking is helpful in getting to the general vicinity of your lost device. But your smartphone or tracker is hidden; finding it may require precision tracking. Many newer trackers like the Pixel Tag come with an ultra-wideband chip that helps you find the exact location of the tracker, given you are nearby. This also works on Pixel smartphones (Pixel 8 Pro series and above) and Samsung Galaxy devices (S21 and above, Plus and Ultra models only).

Recent findings suggest that when using this feature, make sure you have Bluetooth enabled on your smartphone, then open Find Hub. Choose your tracker, and tap Find Nearby. Follow the on-screen instructions to locate the nearby device. You can also tap Play Sound to make the location process easier.

If you think your Android smartphone is lost or stolen, don’t rush to erase all data. While a remote factory reset is great for protecting your data, it also removes the device from your account. It’s best to try to get the device back. Two-factor authentication (or a passkey) on your Google account, along with a biometric lock on your smartphone, will protect the data itself.

According to recent reports, go to the Find Hub website, or use Find Hub on someone else’s phone in guest mode. Choose your device, and instead of Factory Reset, choose Mark as Lost. Here, you’ll see an option to enter a message. Type an alternative contact number, and a message to help recover the device.

#108628. ‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen?

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (984 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Indiewire ↗ Open Full Page

‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the middle of “All of a Sudden,” Mari (Tao Okamoto) pulls out a whiteboard and markers to diagram the principles of nature vs.
  • Recent findings suggest that while a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients.
  • And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is an unorthodox sequence. In the middle of “All of a Sudden,” Mari (Tao Okamoto) pulls out a whiteboard and markers to diagram the principles of nature vs. capitalism for her new friend Marie-Lou (Virginie Efira). The scene lasts 11 minutes and digs into material you would expect in a university seminar, not the latest cinematic achievement from the Oscar-winning director of “Drive My Car,” Ryūsuke Hamaguchi.

Recent findings suggest that while a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients. Related Stories Watch ‘The Sheep Detectives’ VFX Supervisor Break Down the ‘Sheep-Isms’ That Made His Characters Stand Out ‘Filipiñana’ Could Be the Philippines’ First-Ever Oscar-Shortlisted Feature — Even as the Film Was Dealt an Unexpected Tragedy.

And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes. Now, its distributor, Neon, heads into this weekend’s holiday theatrical release believing it has a legit shot at winning over the more commercially oriented Oscar voters — and becoming one of the (increasingly common) foreign-language Best Picture nominations. Neon similarly released “Sentimental Value” and “The Secret Agent” to Best Picture nominations the year before.

Industry observers note that the whiteboard scene is not an extraneous aside, but a critical turning point in the women’s relationship. We asked the film’s writer/director why it not only works, but was deemed vital to the film.

Recent findings suggest that “In trying to answer why this somehow works, I think there’s a few layers to it,” mentioned Hamaguchi while on IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “And one maybe is because it really is something that is far removed from what is generally considered as cinematic. Perhaps because of that, it brings about a certain suspense, where you wonder, ‘OK, what is this for? What is this actually going to do?’ And there’s a certain sense of wondering that happens.”.

The scene comes a little over an hour into the film. Neither woman wants their magical evening to end. Mari follows Marie-Lou to her job as director of a nursing home, where she struggles to implement her passion project, “Huminitude,” a patient-centered care method based on touch and eye contact, which Mari sees in action. What prompts Mari’s whiteboard seminar is an attempt to help her new companion put into perspective the resistance she faces in implementing Huminitude and open the door to problem-solving.

“I think the second part [of why the scene works] really comes down to the efforts of the actors that are performing this scene,” noted Hamaguchi of Okamoto and Efira, who shared the Best Actress Prize at Cannes. “For Tao, I think it was an incredibly difficult scene to perform because first of all she really needed to understand all of the concepts that she was describing here and to really understand everything intellectually. And so in her preparation she did read a lot of the relevant books to really understand what she is talking about.”.

Recent findings suggest that hamaguchi believes the key to his dialogue-driven film is not necessarily how the words are spoken, but the performance of the listening and how the words are received. In Efira’s whiteboard scene, we see a shift from determined frustration to open enthusiasm that changes the direction of the film itself.

“The attitude of listening that Virginie portrays in this moment, I think, is very crucial and really supports this scene,” noted Hamaguchi. “She’s not uninterested in what is going on, but in fact she feels that this is something that she should really be exploring together and she’s there and very much present. And I think this attitude of interest and curiosity really starts to work on the audience as well. And so in that sense I think ultimately this scene really works because of the actors’ performances.”.

One topic that comes up in most post-screening Q&As is that both actresses were not working in the native language. Hamaguchi himself had to work with an interpreter to direct his leads. This is not the first time Hamaguchi has worked this way. On the podcast, he mentioned that, in his experience directing the play inside “Drive My Car,” the language barrier was less of a hindrance and could even aid actors in listening to one another, as shown in the whiteboard scene.

“I felt that, in fact, this kind of difficulty that exists can in fact provide an environment for even more heightened concentration than you might have if you were speaking the same language,” noted Hamaguchi. “ I think that actually when you can actually hear a lot and get a lot of information from somebody’s voice, you can, in fact, precisely feel just how concentrated the person is when they’re saying something by listening to their voice.”.

Asked if any of his collaborators or producers ever questioned the whiteboard scene after reading the script, Hamaguchi noted no, and speculated why: “Because it’s so unusual, I think people understood that this is something that I really wanted to do.”.

According to recent reports, “There were some questions around, ‘This section feels a little long. Is there anything we can do about that?’” recalled Hamaguchi, adding that he made a concerted effort to cut his four-hour script to a three-hour, 16-minute running time.

According to recent reports, “For me, I was ultimately trying to bring in the shortest version that I felt was accurate for this moment. But ultimately, there is this understanding that this moment is a very notable turning point within the film, and so I believe that the producers also understood this.”.

“All of a Sudden” is now playing in select theaters.

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were announced in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

Recent findings suggest that the idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the upcoming version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

It has been revealed that before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

According to recent reports, in iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

That’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

The only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Industry observers note that have you been using iOS 27’s Smart Reply feature in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed.

The annual parade held in New York City is a longtime Thanksgiving staple that airs on NBC during the morning of the holiday. From Spider-Man to Grogu, the floats often feature many beloved pop culture characters, and even hints of what's to come in upcoming projects, including Shrek 5's first look at the ogre's sons last year. As the 100th year of the parade, 2026 marks a particularly notable milestone for the parade.

Due to severe weather, Macy's shared with NBC News that the parade will take place on Saturday, November 28 at 8:30am ET, instead of on Thanksgiving Day this year. A storm with heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding is expected on the day of the actual holiday. Read Macy's official statement about the delay below:.

Recent findings suggest that "The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration. Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, Nov. 28. Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized. We expect the Parade to kick off at 8:30a.m. on Saturday. Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the good news is that “Blade Runner’s” first TV show doesn’t besmirch the franchise’s good name.
  • It has been revealed that not because “Blade Runner 2099” is bad; I want to make it clear upfront this is a solid show, but because, to borrow a phrase from another iconic sci-fi universe, “We were on the verge of greatness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the TV gods are clearly smiling on me. Last year my favorite sci-fi series of all time, “Alien,” was adapted for TV in Hulu’s “Alien: Earth,” and now my second-favorite sci-fi series gets its own small-screen show in the form of Prime Video’s “Blade Runner 2099.”.

According to recent reports, the good news is that “Blade Runner’s” first TV show doesn’t besmirch the franchise’s good name. However, “2099” doesn’t quite manage to live up to the peerless legacy of the 1982 classic and the criminally overlooked 2017 sequel, “Blade Runner 2049.” In fact, frustration was the feeling I felt most keenly while watching the show’s first four episodes (of eight total).

It has been revealed that not because “Blade Runner 2099” is bad; I want to make it clear upfront this is a solid show, but because, to borrow a phrase from another iconic sci-fi universe, “We were on the verge of greatness. We were this close.” This Prime Video original gets so much right that the key areas where it comes up short stick out even more and leave me frustrated with what could have been.

According to recent reports, set 50 years after Ryan Gosling’s Officer K went on the hunt for Harrison Ford’s Rick Deckard, “Blade Runner 2099” leaps forward to a point in the timeline where humanity and replicants have reserved roles. The androids are on top, with humans now treated as second-class citizens, and replicant Blade Runners soon squash any fleeting thoughts of rebellion.

While it’s not the most inspired route to take — a role reversal is hardly an original narrative trope — it does set the stakes appropriately, assuming you as a viewer are rooting for the human race to prevail. Though the moral greyness of the “Blade Runner” series is here, and many replicant characters point out that they’re only doing to humanity what was done to them.

Our leads are Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Replicant Blade Runner just days from retirement (aka impending death), and Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human resistant to the newly introduced world order, pretending to be a Replicant to secure a future for herself and her younger brother. The two soon partner up, forming less of a playful “buddy cop” dynamic and more of an icy, uneasy alliance.

There is intrigue in watching Cora try to remain undetected and in Olwen’s personal plight, as she grapples with her own morality, but despite committed work from Yeoh and Schafer, the overarching narrative threads only threaten to become truly interesting, at least at the midway point. It’s a MacGuffin hunt where the MacGuffin feels barely worth all the trouble.

In a recent development, even when the narrative sputters and gets lost in meandering side quests, at least “Blade Runner 2099” consistently looks phenomenal. The grimy cyberpunk aesthetic of its sci-fi world has been successfully retained in the move from the massive screen to at-home streaming. Visually, it hits all the right notes, and the foreboding score adds to the dark noir atmosphere.

But take my advice, and watch with subtitles; the dialogue audio often fades into the larger soundscape. “Blade Runner 2099” might be the first time in years I’ve had to rewind scenes multiple times just to try and decipher what the characters are actually saying to each other.

Sources indicate that when it comes to production craft, “Blade Runner” is a triumph; it looks absolutely excellent, and sounds great too (well, apart from the dialogue levels). On the surface, it’s every bit the continuation of the “Blade Runner” universe, and as a longtime fan, that was enough to get me invested.

In a recent development, where “2099” struggles is delivering enough narrative momentum to satisfy. Frustratingly early on, large chunks of the episode are a real slog, but to the show’s credit, it’s kept me coming back with well-timed narrative wrinkles. Just when my attention begins to wane, it delivers a precious, spectacular moment when it all comes together, and the clear potential is evident.

According to recent reports, it’s these highs that will keep me watching, and as I move into the back half of the season, I hope the show’s sharpens up and fully realizes its potential. But if I were being truthful, I could see the slow pacing of the early episodes turning more than a few viewers away. “Blade Runner 2099” is in no rush. It asks viewers to be content exploring this fractured world at a crawl.

In a recent development, so, “Blade Runner 2099” isn’t perfect, but the franchise has always ruminated on the flaws of humanity passed down to our own android creations. Maybe the show’s unevenness could be considered poetic. Or maybe I’m just making excuses for a show I want to love more than I do.

Watch "Blade Runner 2099" on Prime Video now.

#108620. HomeKit Weekly: Lafaer’s 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes an annoying automation in Apple Home

HomeKit Weekly: Lafaer’s 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes an annoying automation in Apple Home

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home.
  • HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.
  • A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that indicates up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

“Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

Recent findings suggest that in the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

It has been revealed that it’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

Recent findings suggest that the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts.
  • Sources indicate that airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions.
  • In a recent development, the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

Sources indicate that airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

In a recent development, the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

Sources indicate that if you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

Sources indicate that airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

Sources indicate that I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

It has been revealed that if you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Sources indicate that finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.
