#108613. 10 Hacks Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1237 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Hacks Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1237 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far.
  • I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are important.
  • If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far. The world feels even more detailed and immersive than previous GTA games, which means there's a lot to learn beyond the basic tutorials and prompts the game shares at the beginning. These are the 10 GTA 6 hacks I used to improve the game's quality of life. If you do the same, you'll spend more time immersed in the world, and less time fighting the game's default settings.

I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are important. If you ignore all the optional quests or small asks by other characters, you won't be able to return to those later. These are small things like fixing up the house for Lucia, meditating with her, and buying her a necklace when she asks you to. All of these have an impact on your progress. Take your time in this chapter, and remember to save before starting the mission called "Recalibration." That mission leads to Tourist Trap, which is the point of no return for Chapter 1.

If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different. It's hard to keep an eye on minimap directions while you're also getting used to vehicles in the game, and I used voice navigation to ensure that I don't keep getting lost, particularly for time-sensitive missions. You can enable this by going to GTA VI settings > Audio > GPS Voice > Voice. If you're playing the game on PS5, your DualSense controller's speaker plays GPS voice prompts. This is great as those alerts can be hard to hear over all other in-game sounds from your TV's speaker.

Using GTA 6's default controls, making Jason and Lucia run is quite annoying. The game makes you hold L3 to run, which hurts my thumbs. If you alter movement speed in settings, you can make the characters run just by using the left stick. You can walk by easing off the left stick, or switch to a fast walk, jog, or run when you push the stick all the way. Tweak this by going to GTA VI settings > Gameplay > Movement Speed > Jog. This lets you move faster without draining your stamina. You can also change from Jog to Run if you want the fastest possible movement speed with the left stick. Having said that, my pro tip is to go to Control Scheme in settings, and switch to Classic. This lets you run by holding the X button, as opposed to L3 with default controls.

Haptic strength is one area where GTA 6 takes the immersion a bit too far, as it's dialed up to the maximum level by default. This makes the controller's vibration strength a bit too intense for my liking, and also has a negative impact on battery life. You can fix that by reducing haptic strength a little. It's under GTA VI settings > Controller > Vibration & Haptics Strength.

Many modern controllers develop "stick drift," an glitch where small movements of the analog sticks register as large inputs. This causes a significant problem in games that require precise inputs, such as GTA 6. To counter this potential problem, the game allows you to adjust the deadzone for each analog stick in your controller. That said, this setting can be used to your advantage, even if you don't have stick drift issues in your controller. I recommend dialing up the deadzone to 7 to improve the driving experience. I find most cars in GTA 6 to be a bit floaty to drive, and adjusting the deadzone fixes this issue to a large extent.

According to recent reports, committing a heist attracts heat in GTA 6, and there are many different ways to escape the attention of in-game cops. The usual tricks include stocking up on outfits to change into, parking your vehicle a block or two away, and being so stealthy that you leave no witnesses to your crimes. However, an underrated trick involves using the pickup truck you get at the start of the game. Get a bike in the game, and stash it in your pickup truck. Then, use the truck to drive to the crime scene, and hide the truck a short distance away. Unload the bike, and use it to get to the crime scene. Once the heist is complete, ditch the bike, and run to your truck. Witnesses won't have seen you using the truck, which allows you to escape the area rapidly.

If you are using a car as a getaway vehicle, you can use two tricks to make a smooth escape. First, double-tap the Triangle button to exit your vehicle without switching off its engine. When you return to the vehicle in a hurry, you can escape a lot faster. If you have quick fingers, you can double-tap Triangle first, and just as your character is about to exit the vehicle, press L3 (or X, if you use classic controls). This leaves the car's door open, and saves you a little more time when you're fleeing.

It has been revealed that I suffer from chronic migraines, and I am sensitive to bright lights. Fortunately, GTA 6 has a bunch of accessibility settings that help me play the game for longer. Even if you don't face the same complications, these settings will help reduce eye strain in longer play sessions. Go to GTA VI settings > Display > Flashbang, and switch to Dark. This stops flashbangs from showing a bright white light when they go off. On the same settings page, you can tweak Player Status Effects Intensity to reduce screen effects when your character is low on health or stamina. You can also enable Brightness Reduction to reduce the intensity of bright lights in the game, and try Focus Trail Colorblind Mode if you find it hard to distinguish between different colors.

Industry observers note that I haven't been able to play first-person shooters for decades because the camera movement makes me nauseous and gives me a headache. Of late, I've noticed that it's getting harder to play third-person games too. My first two hours in GTA 6 had me quite worried because I was feeling quite sick, and I had to turn off my PS5. Luckily for me, I found a few tweaks to mitigate this problem. You can do that in GTA VI settings > UI > Persistent Center Dot. This permanently highlights a white dot in the center of the screen, and it reduced my motion sickness enough to help me play the game. You can also go to GTA VI settings > Camera, reduce Camera Bob, and turn off Camera Shake, and Weapon Sway. I also recommend going to the Controller tab in settings, and tweaking all the options under Aim & Look Sensitivity until you find a comfortable level.

GTA 6 includes realistic ringing sounds that linger after explosions in the game. This may be fine for some people, but it can negatively affect some players' gaming sessions. Those who suffer from tinnitus or chronic migraines may not enjoy those ringing sounds, and, luckily, the game allows you to disable them. Open GTA 6's in-game settings, and enable the feature from Audio > Tinnitus Reduction.

Ben Brewster is a filmmaker, critic, screenwriter, and actor whose work sits at the intersection of film culture, craft analysis, and storytelling.

He is a movie list contributing writer at Collider and a contributing writer for High on Films, where he covers contemporary cinema, independent film, and festival releases with an eye toward narrative structure, performance, and visual language.

Ben is an active film festival participant, having worked with Newport Film, the Nantucket Film Festival and as a screener for the Austin, Boston & Woodstock film festivals. He brings to that work a programming instinct shaped by years of close engagement with independent and documentary cinema. This comes with a deep investment in the kinds of films that rarely find their way into the mainstream conversation without someone willing to advocate for them.

Sources indicate that his background spans documentary and narrative filmmaking, film marketing, and production, including work with award-winning directors. This as well as developing his own indie production company, Lilac Creative Studio, through which he develops and produces original work across fiction and nonfiction forms. His debut documentary, Diamond in the Rust, is an examination of economic redevelopment and displacement in the Queens area of New York City. The film was recently accepted to the Unisphere Film Festival, the Defense of Democracy Film Festival, and the Urbanite Arts & Film Festival. This would mark his first festival recognition as a director. In addition to his writing and programming work, Ben hosts Beneath the Bloom, a film podcast exploring the work behind the scenes in cinema, and the struggles one can face to make a movie become a reality. The show reflects the same sensibility that runs through all of his work. A conviction that film is not merely entertainment but one of the most powerful tools human beings have for understanding each other.

Across mediums, his work is driven by a deep belief in film as a communal, transformative art form.

Sources indicate that peanuts has outlasted almost every cartoon on television, and its holiday specials are its bread and butter. Thanksgiving is Thursday, and A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving is streaming only on Apple TV this year, with no traditional linear broadcast airing. However, a new special, Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy, premiered on November 13th, featuring songs from Laufey and John Legend.

It has been revealed that together, the entire library makes the holiday season a perfect time to rank the specials that have built so many family traditions. A note on the choices. I picked specials that critics and viewers both live on and that tie to a date on the calendar. Streaming windows can be quick to change, so check Apple TV before you queue anything up. Spoilers, of course, are not a concern for specials this familiar in the public conversation.

It has been revealed that happy Newly introduced Year, Charlie Brown! starts on the last day of school before Christmas break, when Charlie Brown's teacher assigns a book report on Leo Tolstoy's War and Peace. Charlie Brown ends up dreading his entire vacation, and attempts every shortcut imaginable around reading the novel. He asks a store whether it comes in a variety of different creative forms, including a computer game. Peppermint Patty keeps calling to invite him to her party, and Marcie, Sally, and Lucie get swept up in the drama of it all.

It has been revealed that charlie brings War and Peace to the party and tries to read it on the porch, but he falls asleep and misses the midnight countdown. The Little Red-Haired Girl indicates up and ends up dancing with Linus. But by the end, Charlie finally finishes the book and turns in his report. The special is also a small musical, with songs by Ed Bogas and Desireé Goyette, including a dance lesson number. IMDb users rate the special 7.2, and Collider ranks it third among its best Peanuts specials.

Peppermint Patty spends nearly her entire allowance on eggs in It's the Easter Beagle, Charlie Brown! It is mainly due to the fact Marcie keeps ruining the eggs after she tries to show her how to dye them. She fries the first batch on a griddle, then cracks the next batch before boiling it. Meanwhile, Snoopy tries to find Woodstock a upcoming home and botches that through several different birdhouse attempts. Linus swears the Easter Beagle will hand out eggs, yet Sally doubts him after the Great Pumpkin fiasco.

Sources indicate that on Easter morning, Snoopy turns out to be the Easter Beagle. He distributes eggs, including one for Lucy, but runs out before reaching Charlie Brown. The special earned an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Children's Special, and CBS aired it every Easter from 1974 till 2000. Peppermint Patty's exasperated shouts became a running gag moment. IMDb consumers rate it at 7.5. Its plot is a little thin, but the visual gags, such as Snoopy's dance in a department store, foster memorable moments. Todd Barbee voiced Charlie Brown for the final time, and Linda Ercoli played Peppermint Patty.

According to recent reports, charlie Brown incessantly checks his mailbox over and over in Be My Valentine, convinced that one is on the way. Like the Easter Beagle episode, this one aired on CBS for 25 years. At school, Charlie arrives with a briefcase to carry all the cards and love he expects to get. Snoopy builds an elaborate music box valentine and stages a puppet show about love. Linus, has a massive crush on his teacher, Miss Othmar. He buys her a huge box of chocolates before learning later on she has left with her boyfriend.

According to recent reports, sally mistakes the gift for her own and makes Linus a valentine in return. Unfortunately for Charlie yet again, he ends the day with a single candy heart that reads, "Forget it, kid." Linus chucks the chocolates he got off a bridge, where Snoopy and Woodstock are positioned to catch and eat them. After the special first aired, children across the country sent valentines to Charlie Brown. Violet's used valentine and Snoopy's surprise kiss give the special a bittersweet ending. A follow-up, A Charlie Brown Valentine, was released in 2002, and IMDb owners rated the original 7.3.

Charlie Brown's All-Stars! was the first Peanuts special not constructed around a holiday. After Charlie Brown's baseball team quits on him after another loss, he finds himself at his lowest. The hardware store owner, Mr. Hennessy, offers to sponsor the team, put them in an organized league, and buy them real uniforms. The kids rush back, but Charlie Brown soon realizes that the league does not allow girls or dogs. He's then forced to choose between the upcoming gear, and his loyalty to Lucy, Violet, Patty, Frieda, and Snoopy.

It has been revealed that charlie turns down the offer and keeps the secret until after the game. It, of course, leaves his team enraged after they lose. Schroeder finally scolds the girls for their selfishness, and they make Charlie Brown a uniform from Linus's blanket. Yahoo ranks the special fifth among the Peanuts episodes, and IMDb people rate it at 7.5. A Record Store Day release with music from the special is scheduled for November 27th, and the uniform storyline returned in a 1996 remake. The moral decision gives Charlie Brown one of his most admirable moments.

A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving premiered on CBS on November 20th, 1973. It begins when Peppermint Patty invites herself and her friends over to Charlie Brown's for dinner. Charlie is forced to improvise a meal. Snoopy, Woodstock, and Linus help him prepare a feast of toast, pan-fried popcorn, pretzel sticks, jelly beans, and sundaes. Patty rejects the meal for lacking traditional values and foods, until Marcie reminds her that she invited herself.

In a recent development, rotten Tomatoes lists A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving at 67% from critics and 76% from audiences, a modest score for a special that families consistently rewatch every year. Linus tells the story of the first Thanksgiving along the way, while Snoopy and Woodstock's more traditional meal back at the doghouse adds a touch of sweetness. Peppermint Patty later asks Marcie to apologize for her, an echo of The Courtship of Miles Standish, and then apologizes directly.

Industry observers note that in It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, Linus keeps a lonely vigil in a pumpkin patch, certain that the Great Pumpkin will rise. Apple describes the special as Charlie Brown prepping for a party, Snoopy setting his sights on the Red Baron, and Linus awaiting a miracle. Sally joins Linus and misses the party, which leads to one of the funniest rants in the series. Snoopy's Flying Ace sequence turns a doghouse into a World War I airplane.

It has been revealed that the special marked its 60th anniversary this year, which ends with Charlie Brown returning home from trick or treating with a bag of rocks. Rotten Tomatoes lists it at 90% from critics and 85% from audiences. Yahoo's ranking of the Peanuts specials put it first and calls it the best Halloween cartoon ever. After it aired, children across the nation sent candy to Charlie Brown and Vince Guaraldi's score includes The Great Pumpkin Waltz.

Sources indicate that A Charlie Brown Christmas opens with Charlie feeling down and depressed about the commercialism of the holiday. Charles M. Schulz wrote it, Bill Melendez directed, and Lee Mendelsohn produced. It aired on CBS every year from 1965 till 2000, and then through ABC until 2019. Lucy asks Charlie to direct the gang's Christmas play, and he buys a small, scrawny tree that his friends end up mocking. The special used real child voice actors and left out a laugh track. These were choices that worried CBS mightily at the time, before it won an Emmy and a Peabody Award.

Sources indicate that snoopy decorates his doghouse for a contest, and Linus calmly recites the Christmas story from the Gospel of Luke. Vince Guaraldi's jazz score, including Linus and Lucy and Christmastime Is Here, became as famous as the special itself. Rotten Tomatoes lists it at 86% from critics and 93% from audiences. The 61st anniversary falls on December 9th.

What makes the Helix Midnight Luxe the best side-sleeper mattress we’ve tested — straight from the co-founder who engineered it

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was 2013, and future Helix Sleep co-founders Adam Tishman, Jerry Lin and Kristian von Rickenbach had a simple mission: to find a comfy latest mattress that wouldn't break the bank.

But instead of an enjoyable shopping experience, the trio were faced with confusing online cliches, or pricey mattresses from brick and mortar stores.

Quickly, an opportunity sprung up in front of them: to disrupt a tired industry and subsequently create one of America's leading sleep brands.

Fast forward to present day and Helix Sleep is making some of the best mattresses we've tested, chief among them being the Helix Midnight Luxe, which is currently 25% off at Helix.

In an exclusive interview for Tom's Guide, Helix co-founder Jerry Lin talks us through the conception, creation and rebirth of the Midnight Luxe, our top-rated mattress for side sleepers, and what the future looks like for this award-wining bed.

In a recent development, the Midnight Luxe is always included in the monthly Helix mattress sale, but this month's discount is higher than normal. For Black Friday you can save 25% on every size, with a queen costing $1,874 (was $2,498). You'll also get a year's sleep trial, lifetime warranty, and free shipping.

Tishman, Lin and von Rickenbach identified three major problems when trying to buy a upcoming mattress:.

According to recent reports, the trio started working with sleep PHD researchers in Europe to design a line of mattresses that weren't one-size-fits-all, but instead distinguishable by sleep position. (And by looking closely at our sleep DNA, the brand name Helix was born.).

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

According to recent reports, when Helix Sleep finally launched in 2015, they did so with a direct-to-consumer model. They sought to demystify the mattress buying process by creating bespoke mattresses based on your answers to the Helix Sleep quiz.

After thousands of online orders, in 2017 the brand mined the sleep quiz data to roll out a basic range of mattresses that catered to every major sleep position.

Sources indicate that soon after, the original Helix Midnight entered the online marketplace. Now the entry level bed in the brand's expanded range, the Core Midnight is designed to meet the needs of a typical side sleeper; cushioning at the shoulders, hips and knees, and support at the lower back.

In terms of mattress firmness, we'd rate the Core Midnight as a medium. It was a great start for improved side sleep comfort, but the best was yet to come...

In 2018, Helix Sleep introduced the Luxe Collection. Maintaining its philosophy of mattresses tailored for every individual sleep need, this upcoming and more luxurious range of beds aimed to elevate the comfort of the Core mattresses to appeal to customers seeking a truly indulgent sleep.

The original inspiration was straightforward: take the medium-feel of our original Helix Midnight and elevate it with the comfort, materials, and craftsmanship you'd expect from a luxury hotel mattress.

“The Helix Luxe Collection is our most popular mattress line, with the Midnight Luxe consistently ranking as our best-selling model,” reveals Lin, a Wharton MBA who began his career in investment banking.

“The original inspiration was straightforward: take the medium-feel, side-sleeper-friendly design of our original Helix Midnight and elevate it with the comfort, materials, and craftsmanship you'd expect from a luxury hotel mattress, but at a much more accessible price point.".

It has been revealed that the timing of the 2018 launch couldn’t have been better. With original mattress-in-a-box brands Casper and Purple disrupting the traditional brick-and-mortar mattress industry, Helix and its Luxe line became an integral part of the growing boxed bed revolution.

Then, just two years later, many parts of the States found themselves under stay-at-home orders as part of Covid-19 quarantine measures.

One of Helix's biggest competitive advantages is that we manufacture our own foam.

With 'work from bed' the new normal for many Americans, and with little else to spend hard-earned cash on, the e-commerce mattress industry boomed.

Some even reported that the Helix Midnight Luxe was the only thing helping them sleep during those uncertain times.

With the bed-to-door industry on fast forward, Helix wanted to keep the Midnight Luxe ahead of the curve. The answer lay in doubling down: improving the mattress from base to quilted cover.

The Midnight Luxe stands at 13.5" tall and is crafted from a combination of coils and comfort foam.

Each layer serves a specific purpose for its overall sleep comfort.

From top to bottom, let's take a closer look at the Luxe's overall structure:.

It has been revealed that A soft, breathable cover sits above two layers of premium quilting foam (1.5 lb and gel-infused 1.8 lb), creating a plush sleep surface that's both comfortable and durable. The standard cover is made with TENCEL fabric.

In a recent development, an additional layer of gel memory foam provides targeted pressure relief, particularly around the shoulders and hips, making the Midnight Luxe especially well-suited for side sleepers. This gel memory foam has an IFD (Indentation Force Deflection) of 10-18 and a density of 1.8-4.0 PCF.

Industry observers note that helix's signature titanium, graphite, and copper infused memory foam delivers deeper contouring and is engineered for temperature management and long-term durability. It has a 4lb foam density, which is more than double the 2lb density of many foams used by standard brands.

Industry observers note that next, A firmer transition layer, with lower density foam, creates a gradual shift from the plush comfort layers to the supportive coil system underneath. This helps prevent the sensation of sinking too deeply into the mattress.

It has been revealed that up to 1,000 individually wrapped eight-inch coils provide responsive support, with enhanced reinforcement in the lumbar region to help promote healthy spinal alignment. Reinforced perimeter coils also improve edge support, making the full surface of the mattress more usable. Each coil is made from tempered steel and wrapped in polypropylene non-woven fabric.

The Helix Midnight Luxe is a luxury hybrid mattress. While the coils are in crucial factor in the bed's overall comfort layer, it is the proprietary foams that help set this boxed bed apart from many competitors.

While most brands use pre-poured foams from third party suppliers, Helix manufacture their own foam (more on this below). This should allow them to fine tune its construction until the optimal level of comfort is achieved. A feat I think they've pulled it off.

As someone who sleeps predominantly on my side and occasionally on my back, I feel as though the Helix Midnight Luxe has been crafted specifically for me in way that I haven't experienced while testing another mattress.

The foams provide just the right amount of body-contouring support across the shoulders, hips and knees, while holding the spine in healthy alignment with the rest of the body.

Recent findings suggest that in 2022, Helix merged with sleep brand Brooklyn Bedding. Now operating from its own factory in Arizona, Helix began experimenting with pouring and manufacturing its own mattress foam, alongside its own coils.

This decision proved to be a pivotal moment in the development of the Midnight Luxe.

“One of Helix's biggest competitive advantages is something most consumers never see: we manufacture our own foam,” explains Lin, who built the finance and operations backbone behind Helix’s growth and helps steer the brand’s product innovation and retail expansion.

“Many mattress brands are essentially assemblers. They source foam, coils, and other components from third-party suppliers and combine them into a finished product.

“At Helix, we take a different approach. We manufacture our core components ourselves, giving us significantly more control over material quality, performance, and cost.

“A perfect example is the proprietary memory foam we developed specifically for the Luxe Collection.”.

We developed a high-density, 4lb memory foam infused with titanium, graphite and copper.

Sources indicate that “For the latest Midnight Luxe, we developed a high-density, 4lb memory foam infused with titanium, graphite and copper,” explains Lin. “This is one of the most crucial innovations in the redesigned mattress.”.

Industry observers note that foam density is an crucial factor in overall durability. Higher-density memory foams can offer greater resistance to daily use, wear and compression, helping the Midnight Luxe to maintain its comfort and support through years of use.

And with a queen costing in the region of $1,900 when not on sale, durability is crucial.

However, as someone who has tested both versions of the Helix Midnight Luxe, it's worth noting that the trade off of this durability is that the 2025 redesigned model is slightly firmer.

"At 4lb per cubic foot, this is a premium-density memory foam engineered for long-term performance," explains Lin.

For context, many luxury manufacturer's use foams under 2lb in density, with 1.8lb considered an acceptable density.

Sources indicate that helix also incorporates three distinct materials into the foam formulation, each selected for its specialist properties. These are:.

By manufacturing its own foam, the brand can refine density, responsiveness and body-cradling characteristics until it's achieved the desired balance.

For the Midnight Luxe in particular, that means "deep pressure relief without sacrificing the support that makes the [mattress] so comfortable," states Lin.

"It's a level of material customization that would be much more difficult if we were simply purchasing off-the-shelf foam.".

“While the deeper comfort layers are vital, we also paid attention to the part of the mattress you feel first: the quilted pillow top,” says Lin.

"The plush pillow top is a quilted comfort system made with two layers of high-density foam, a 1.5lb layer and a 1.8lb gel-infused layer.

“These layers are designed to provide immediate cushioning and pressure relief, particularly around sensitive areas like the shoulders and hips.".

While pressure relief is a crucial feature of any mattress designed specifically for side sleepers, there was another reason the brand invested in higher-density materials at the top — durability.

Recent findings suggest that "The uppermost layers of a mattress experience significant daily compression and wear," explains Lin. "Using higher-quality foam in these layers helps the Midnight Luxe to maintain its comfort characteristics over time.

"By incorporating 1.5lb and 1.8lb foams, we're making a deliberate investment in materials that go beyond what's commonly used in the industry.".

For context, both the Saatva Classic, the highest-scoring mattress we've ever tested, and the DreamCloud Classic, our second highest ranking mattress overall because of its superb value for money, use a foam density of 1.4lb in their Euro top covers, which are inherently different by design to the plush pillow top on the Midnight Luxe.

According to recent reports, the Helix Midnight Luxe launched in 2018 as a luxury hotel-style upgrade to the original Midnight (now marketed as the Core Midnight). It has a plush pillow top and zoned lumbar support for back pain relief.

"Those features helped establish the Luxe Collection as our most popular mattress line," states Lin.

"But as our manufacturing capabilities evolved, we saw an opportunity to make more meaningful improvements to the mattress itself.".

In 2025, Helix introduced the most significant redesign of the Luxe Collection since its launch.

Rather than focusing on cosmetic changes or additional features, they sought to reengineer the mattress from the inside out.

"These improvements reflect how we think about product development at Helix," claims Lin.

"We're constantly looking for ways to improve the actual sleep experience, whether that's through better pressure relief, more consistent support, improved temperature regulation, or materials that maintain their performance longer.

"Ultimately, our philosophy is simple: a luxury mattress should be defined by the quality of what's inside it, not just how it looks or how much it costs," concludes Lin.

"That's what guided the latest Midnight Luxe redesign, and it's what continues to drive our approach to mattress innovation.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the newly introduced S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

The newly introduced Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the newly introduced health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:.

Recent findings suggest that the complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a newly introduced Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Recent findings suggest that most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:.

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off promptly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

Have you upgraded to Apple Watch Series 12? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

10 Movie Families We'd Never Want To Spend Thanksgiving With, Ranked

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rewatching classic movies is also a common trend on Thanksgiving and the days before and after the holiday, and that’s somewhat ironic given the family drama that often happens in movies like these.
  • In a recent development, many of these movies, whether they be big franchises or holiday classics (or both), feature some severely dysfunctional families.
  • There are many contenders for the most chaotic and dysfunctional of families in film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rewatching classic movies is also a common trend on Thanksgiving and the days before and after the holiday, and that’s somewhat ironic given the family drama that often happens in movies like these. The same goes for classic holiday movies like National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation, Home Alone, and more. But though these family-centric movies can make for great viewing on Thanksgiving, the characters they follow may not make the best organization themselves.

In a recent development, many of these movies, whether they be big franchises or holiday classics (or both), feature some severely dysfunctional families. Star Wars is a prime example of this, as the chaotic Skywalker family are central to the entire story of the galaxy. The Marvel franchise has a similar story with Vision, Wanda, and their two twin boys, a complicated dynamic that was once again explored in the recently concluded VisionQuest.

There are many contenders for the most chaotic and dysfunctional of families in film. The Skywalkers are right up there, of course, as are the Griswolds, but families in movies like Knives Out, Ready or Not, and more are all in the mix as well.

The Simpsons are an incredibly conflicting family. On the one hand, they are wholesome and genuinely care about one another. On the other hand, they are constantly at each other’s throats (sometimes quite literally, as Homer chokes Bart). Ultimately, the Simpsons aren’t as inhospitiable as some of their contemporaries, but they certainly wouldn’t make great Thanksgiving guests either (especially Homer, a character who is seemingly always followed by chaos).

Sources indicate that the Dursleys are the family that Harry Potter lives with before he comes to Hogwarts, and during the summers in between school years as well. They are extremely cruel to Harry, forcing him to remain cooped up in a closet turned into a bedroom. They also favor their own child, Dudley, to an extreme degree, making Harry feel left out in comparison. At the same time, the Dursleys are also shown to be rude and conniving at the dinner table, which is the last thing anyone would want to deal with at Thanksgiving.

Recent findings suggest that the Wayne family in Joaquin Phoenix’s Joker would also be high on the list of people to avoid over Thanksgiving. That’s because Arthur Fleck may or may not be the secret child of Thomas Wayne, making him and Bruce Wayne brothers. Thomas Wayne vehemently denies this and even gets violent with Arthur when he brings it up. Arthur himself is also extremely disturbed and violent, which makes this version of the Waynes an unpredictable and dangerous bunch.

It has been revealed that the Thrombeys are some of the most complex characters in recent film history. Writer and director Rian Johnson crafted characters that felt like real people, all of whom have lived very complicated lives. That realism and believability plays into why the Thrombey family would be horrible guests at the Thanksgiving table.

Sources indicate that at the end of the day, virtually every member of the Thrombey family was after the grand inheritance. Some made their pursuits more obvious than others, but they boiled down to the same kind of person, searching for money and power, and willing to do almost anything for money.

Even the seemingly nicer members of the family, like Meg Thrombey (Katherine Langford), were still acting in their own self-interests at the end of the day. Then there’s Ransom (Chris Evans), who went so far as to commit murder, which makes this family less than ideal guests at the dinner table.

It has been revealed that as far as forgetful parents go, Kate and Peter McCallister take the cake. They are the mother and father in Home Alone and its sequel, Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, and their son is young Kevin McCallister, who very famously was left behind twice. That forgetfulness (or, perhaps more accurately, outright neglect) would make them awkward Thanksgiving dinner guests.

However, the McCallisters are also extremely frantic and chaotic when they interact with one another. At the beginning of Home Alone, family members are shown screaming at one another, often from other floors. They’re also incredibly antagonistic, such as Kevin’s brother Buzz, who bullies him relentlessly. The McCallisters may be wholesome at times, but they certainly bring their fair share of baggage, too.

It has been revealed that arguably even more chaotic is the Griswold family from National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation. What makes this family so chaotic is that there are multiple generations all attending the same holiday gathering. Some of the older ones, for example, can barely see or hear, which makes for some truly awkward interactions during the family dinner. Then there’s Randy Quaid’s character and his section of the family, who seemingly lack all social skills and basic manners.

As far as families go, there aren’t many more complicated or disturbing than the Le Domas’ from Ready or Not. The family’s troubles began when their ancestor, Vincent Le Domas, struck a deal with the devil, thus giving him and future generations infinite wealth and success. However, this comes at a huge cost, as the family must engage in a deadly wedding game whenever a fresh member joins.

Sources indicate that that makes them some of the very worst people to attend Thanksgiving dinner with. After all, they pose a huge threat to new members of their family, and they prove in Ready or Not that they are more than willing and capable of committing serious acts of violence. Not only that, but they also seem to enjoy it, too, which makes them high on the list of families to avoid.

The Skywalkers aren’t the only chaotic family in a galaxy far, far away. There’s also the Palpatine family, which consists of Sheev Palpatine (aka the Emperor), his son Dathan and his wife Miramir, and the Jedi Rey (aka Rey Skywalker). The source of this family’s chaos is the patriarch Sheev Palpatine, who is arguably the most evil person to have ever lived in the Star Wars galaxy.

Industry observers note that sheev was responsible for murdering billions of people all across the galaxy, not only with war and oppression, but with the Death Star and Death Star II as well. Palpatine also used his son as a means to live forever, and planned on doing the same with his granddaughter. Clearly, they all have a lot of baggage, which would make any gathering with them in attendance likely extremely awkward.

In terms of horror movies, few families feel as dysfunctional and disturbed as the Grahams in Hereditary. The death of young Charlie Graham created a rift in the family that they ultimately weren’t able to overcome, as they fell victim to a villainous devil cult. In the end, Peter Graham becomes a vessel for the devil (or a demon), and that’s pretty much the last person anyone would want to have for Thanksgiving.

Industry observers note that the family to avoid the most at Thanksgiving, by far, is the Skywalkers. There are several generations here, from Shmi Skywalker to Anakin and Padme, then Luke and Leia (and Han Solo, via marriage), and now Ben Solo, aka Kylo Ren. Not only are there multiple generations, but each is deeply affected by trauma, too. After all, Anakin Skywalker turned to the dark side of the Force and fought against his kids several times.

Luke and Leia (perhaps surprisingly) turned out okay, but Ben Solo followed in his grandfather’s footsteps. He even went so far as to kill his father, Han Solo. Ultimately, there’s far too much baggage in the Skywalker family for them to have a successful Thanksgiving with one another.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, editor's Note: The following contains spoilers for the entire season of Blade Runner 2099.Blade Runner 2099 is officially out — the thrilling eight-episode series from creator/showrunner Silka Luisa drops today on Prime Video. The series takes place 50 years after Blade Runner 2049 and 90 years after the Ridley Scott film. 2099 introduces us to a version of Los Angeles we've never seen before — one run by replicants. We meet Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human working undercover as a replicant Blade Runner. Hiding in plain sight, Cora slowly learns the truth behind this replicant-run world while partnered with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Blade Runner who is dying within a matter of days.

The series takes Cora and Olwen across Los Angeles, ultimately leading them to discover that what they're hunting for is the truth of the Nexus-1 replicants. Cora learns that her adoptive mother, Helena (Sheila Atim) was one of the original replicants, born alongside Julius (Tom Burke), who eventually killed her while hunting for Tyrell's memory, which hold the secret to creating more Nexus-1 replicants. The series ends ambiguously, with Cora returning to the LAPD after Julius' death and Olwen journeying off to space, uncertain whether she's set to discover latest worlds or simply finish off the last remaining days of her life.

Sources indicate that collider spoke with both Schafer and Yeoh about that surprising Blade Runner 2099 finale. The two actors discuss their characters' changing relationships and what leads Cora to protecting Olwen in that final fight against Julius. Yeoh also breaks down that thrilling fight with Clotilde (Amy Lennox) and why that scene was so important for Olwen. Schafer contemplates Cora's final conversation with Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey), and what it might mean for the two humans caught in a world full of replicants.

In a recent development, COLLIDER: One of the scenes I really liked in the finale is seeing Cora protecting Olwen from Julius; I thought that was such a great scene to show the development of their relationship. Can you guys talk about developing that bond between these two characters and going from enemies to these close friends?

HUNTER SCHAFER: Yeah. I mean, it was so magical, as we were getting to know each other as we were getting to know our own respective characters better throughout the filming process; it sort of coincided with the growth of Cora and Olwen's relationship. I think it was a matter of exploring it; I think moments would reveal themselves as more human or intimate with us, depending on the nature of the scene. But I really loved... I mean, especially by Episode 6 when they're really seeing each other for who they are; from then there's a beauty to the mutual understanding.

MICHELLE YEOH: I think the most important thing is that there were no more secrets. Because at the beginning, she had her secrets. She was like a bloody human trying to pretend to be a replicant! That's horrifying for Olwen, who is the replicant who thinks she knows everything and knows what it takes to be a replicant and to be lied to by someone like that.

Recent findings suggest that but, at that point, when we came to confront each other and then finally understand that we both had secrets that we kept from each other, and that secrets freed us and made our bond stronger and made us work together, because we were on the same mission, right? We needed to find what was the answer that could destroy this very fragile place that we have. So I think it was important as a human and as a replicant, we have to work together; otherwise, everything will go to hell.

Along the way, they have learned in very strange ways to care for each other, and that bond was beautiful, because, right at the end, it was like, we fought for each other, not just with each other, but at the end it was how to defend ourselves. So I don't think Cora at any point would not jump in front if she felt Olwen was in trouble.

SCHAFER: Yeah, there's a real kinship by the end.

Recent findings suggest that michelle, you have this great scene where Olwen's fighting Clotilde, and she has the chance to let her fall to her death. Why do you think that she takes that moment and saves her? Because, obviously, that comes in to benefit her later on, but, at that moment, she could just let her die.

YEOH: I know, I think this is almost like a flashback to Roy Batty and Deckard at that point, where it's like, what is humanity? Does it mean that if you were born as a replicant, you can't find the humanity, you don't understand it? And, at that point, you're right, Olwen could have let her go, because she was getting so badly beaten up by Clotilde. I mean, she could have just [been] like, "Die, you bitch," you know? [Laughs] And then I can just move on to do other things. But then that's what it takes to be human. To save another, whether it's someone who doesn't have a soul or has a soul or whatever it is, but not to just let someone die. And I think that was the humanity that suddenly struck Olwen, and she didn't let go, which then also transferred to Clotilde, because otherwise she would not have had clarity in her head.

SCHAFER: Yeah, they both had desires to live.

YEOH: Yes, and also desires to know the truth. Like, what is this guy Julius selling us? Because he's the one that's like, "I gave you this. This is what you could have. You would come back, and you'd be stronger, and you wouldn't have to die." It was a very special moment in that scene which just turned things around.

According to recent reports, hunter, for you, Cora has that final scene with Greta, and I think it's just such an intriguing moment, especially since I really love Greta in the show. What's your read on what's happening there between these two people?

Recent findings suggest that SCHAFER: I think Blade Runner is famous for its open-ended conclusions in that they are open to interpretation, but I think Cora sees herself in Greta. And Greta is such an intriguing character, in another way, I think, as a human who has infiltrated the LAPD in that world of Blade Runners. Greta is a human as well. So, I think there's a kinship that she feels there, even though they've barely spoken. They've only really done a few empathy tests together and had a few interactions, but human-to-human, there still is that connection together.

In a recent development, YEOH: Yeah, that poor human was actually quite a sad figure because she's forced to be there because she has a gift of being able to detect. And I think she detected that in Cora at the beginning because she sort of reached out to call for help, like help me get away from this.

SCHAFER: Well, yeah, I love that because you're not just part of the test, or if it's really her.

Recent findings suggest that YEOH: Yeah, exactly! And that was like, whoa! Is Cora going to "fall for it"? Is it real? That was so cool.

SCHAFER: And then she drops her face, and Cora passes the test; it's awesome.

Blade Runner 2099 is now streaming on Prime Video.

I used to take my AirPods Max with me on planes, but lately, I've been fine with just my Pros, since the noise cancellation seemingly blocks just about as much background sound as my over-the-ear headphones. Equally great are both the transparency modes, which pump in outside sounds while you're wearing your AirPods, and Adaptive Transparency, which automatically adjusts the level of transparency based on how loud or soft your surroundings are. This is a great mode for wearing your AirPods in loud environments, so you can still hear everything without the noise becoming overwhelming. To that point, these AirPods are actually FDA-certified hearing aids.

There are plenty of other features available here as well, especially if you have a compatible iPhone. AirPods Pro 3 have a built-in heart rate sensor, so you can track workouts without an Apple Watch; you can translate conversations in real time with Live Translate; "Conversation Awareness" lowers the volume of your audio and turns on transparency mode when you start speaking; and they run for eight hours on one charge with noise cancellation enabled.

This isn't an in-depth list of the AirPods Pro 3's set of features. But suffice it to say, these earbuds are worth their full MSRP of $249. So not only can I wholeheartedly recommend them at $149, but I'd say they're an easy buy if you've been thinking about picking up AirPods for yourself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that 9to5Mac is brought to you by Tello Mobile. Switching to Tello Mobile can bring the cost of your blueprint down to as little as $5 a month, or an unlimited plan for just $25 a month, all on America’s largest 5G network. See all of the available intends at tello.com.

Among iOS 27’s many latest features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces significant AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting fresh features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the enhancement also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:.

Recent findings suggest that after iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

In a recent development, to move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Sources indicate that most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

I feel like I’m exactly who this feature was made for. After years of running dual SIM, I now have a personal line on my Duo and work line on an 18 Pro. Going out with friends, family, etc, I’d love to bring one phone again while bringing both numbers with me, but keeping work system access to a specific, separate device. Only current problem is waiting for Verizon to activate the feature and then see if it actually works well.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”.

#108599. Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2883 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The AI pioneer notes it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to substantial problems.
  • Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.
  • According to recent reports, andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer notes it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to substantial problems.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

According to recent reports, andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he notes he has identified the next significant shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

Ng’s current efforts are focused on his organization Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he claims can yield “small data” solutions to big issues in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

The great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

Recent findings suggest that andrew Ng: This is a massive question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

Ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a newly introduced paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

Ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

According to recent reports, having remarked that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of users, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing organization with millions of customers.

Ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

Industry observers note that I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and noted, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

Sources indicate that over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing upcoming here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

Ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and said, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

The data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one company or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that revealed up.

In a recent development, you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

Ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

According to recent reports, when you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand upcoming model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having said that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For significant data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

According to recent reports, for example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very swiftly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

It has been revealed that could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

Ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. Upcoming tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an key piece of the puzzle.

According to recent reports, one of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

Ng: In AI, data cleaning is vital, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention swiftly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

For example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

Recent findings suggest that ng: I think synthetic data is an notable tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

“In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion people. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

Synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

In a recent development, to make these issues more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a tech giant approaches Landing AI and says it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

In a recent development, ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

It has been revealed that one of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

How do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

Industry observers note that ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift matter. I find it really vital to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and revision the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

Recent findings suggest that in the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion consumers. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

In a recent development, ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent latest neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s important for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

Ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

This article appears in the April 2022 print issue as “Andrew Ng, AI Minimalist.”.

Why Black Friday Is the Perfect Time to Start a Gym Membership

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (768 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that most people are probably waiting until Jan.
  • The week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit.
  • Sources indicate that this week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a new air fryer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the fresh year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

The week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on latest tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

Sources indicate that this week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a new air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for fresh Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

Deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

Try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

Recent findings suggest that be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

In a recent development, gyms also run sales around New Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

Industry observers note that that's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're latest. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

From Black Friday to New Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Recent findings suggest that prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K initiative works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your New Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

This is also the season when many workplaces and health aims wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some prepares include gym memberships or discounts.

HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before New Year's resolution time arrives.
